+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("a-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("b-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("c-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("z-free")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("cz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("nz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("ba")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("bb")), ("root", id("b-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("bc")), ("root", id("c-blocked"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let wrapped_removed: u64 = (0..4).map(|_| store.sweep_server_at(10, 1).unwrap()).sum();
+    assert_eq!(wrapped_removed, 1, "continuation reaches the free root within one bounded turn per due root");
+    assert!(store.raw_rows("cascadeKids").is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(store.raw_rows("nullableKids")[0].field("root").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Null);
+
+    // The cursor is after z. A lower new key is found after the scan wraps;
+    // each restricted root still consumes one bounded visit.
+    store.seed_server_at([("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", id("aa-free")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10)),
+    ]))], 0).unwrap();
+    let wrapped_removed: u64 = (0..4).map(|_| store.sweep_server_at(10, 1).unwrap()).sum();
+    assert_eq!(wrapped_removed, 1, "a wrapped scan reaches the new lower key within one bounded turn per due root");
+    assert!(!store.raw_rows("roots").iter().any(|row| row.field("id").unwrap() == &id("aa-free")));
+}
+
 #[test] fn reference_actions_memory() { run(&mut Memory::new()); }
 #[test] fn reference_actions_sqlite() { run(&mut Sqlite::new("reference-actions")); }
 
diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-sim/tests/expiry_reference_actions.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-sim/tests/expiry_reference_actions.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..05a91f6ddf
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-sim/tests/expiry_reference_actions.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,140 @@
+//! Expiry is a physical delete trigger for referential actions (LLP 3000.039
+//! §3). These cases cover scheduled cleanup, commit-end retirement and
+//! same-id replacement of an expired row against the real engine.
+use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState, value::object};
+use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+
+fn id(value: &str) -> Value { Value::Id(value.into()) }
+
+fn engine(source: &str) -> Engine {
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap()
+}
+
+const SWEEP: &str = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+  sync public
+table cascadeKids:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'cascade kids'
+  sync public
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+  sync public
+table blockers:
+  root: roots
+  public 'blockers'
+  sync public
+"#;
+
+#[test]
+fn sweep_applies_every_action_and_advances_past_a_restricted_root() {
+    let mut e = engine(SWEEP);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("a-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("b-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("c-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("z-free")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("ca")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("cz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("nz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("ba")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("bb")), ("root", id("b-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("bc")), ("root", id("c-blocked"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+
+    for expected in [0, 0, 0, 1] {
+        assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 1).unwrap(), expected, "a one-row sweep must advance its physical scan position");
+    }
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["a-blocked", "b-blocked", "c-blocked"]);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["ca"]);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+
+    for blocker in ["ba", "bb", "bc"] { e.seed_delete("blockers", blocker).unwrap(); }
+    assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 10).unwrap(), 3);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn a_late_cascade_refusal_rolls_back_earlier_set_null_writes() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 1 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 1 by root
+  public 'children'
+table grandchildren:
+  child: children
+  read through .child
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("p")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("n")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+        ("children".into(), object([("id", id("c")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+        ("grandchildren".into(), object([("id", id("g")), ("child", id("c"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+
+    let error = e.sweep_expired(10, 10).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", "{error:?}");
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &id("p"), "the prior set-null write rolled back");
+    for table in ["roots", "children", "grandchildren"] {
+        assert_eq!(e.store().rows(table).unwrap().len(), 1, "{table}");
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn commit_retirement_and_expired_same_id_replacement_apply_actions() {
+    let source = format!(r#"{SWEEP}
+mutation bornExpired():
+  insert roots {{id: 'born', expiresAt: now}}
+  insert cascadeKids {{id: 'born-c', root: 'born'}}
+  insert nullableKids {{id: 'born-n', root: 'born'}}
+  return null
+mutation bornRestricted():
+  insert roots {{id: 'blocked', expiresAt: now}}
+  insert blockers {{id: 'blocked-b', root: 'blocked'}}
+  return null
+mutation replaceExpired():
+  insert roots {{id: 'old', expiresAt: null}}
+  return null
+"#);
+    let mut e = engine(&source);
+    let sent = e.mutate("bornExpired", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(sent.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", sent.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+
+    let refused = e.mutate("bornRestricted", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(refused.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_REFERENCED"), "{:?}", refused.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty(), "the refused birth and its blocker roll back together");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("blockers").unwrap().is_empty());
+
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("old")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(1))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("old-c")), ("root", id("old"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let replaced = e.mutate("replaceExpired", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(replaced.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", replaced.state);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap()[0].field("expiresAt").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty(), "same-id cleanup cannot orphan the expired predecessor's child");
+}
diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..c6754a981f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,175 @@
+//! A store written by the frozen 0.4.28 binary adopts digest-addressed
+//! aggregate rows before the current engine serves it.
+use rusqlite::Connection;
+use std::{
+    fs,
+    path::{Path, PathBuf},
+    process::Command,
+};
+
+const SOURCE: &str = r#"use personas alice
+table entries:
+  group: text <=256
+  amount: int
+  insert <- allow
+  public
+view totals: sum entries of .amount by .group
+  public
+mutation add(group: text <=256, amount: int):
+  insert entries {group, amount}
+query total(group: text <=256):
+  return totals[group]
+"#;
+
+struct Temp(PathBuf);
+impl Temp {
+    fn new() -> Self {
+        let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
+            "snapback4-maintained-id-{}-{}",
+            std::process::id(),
+            std::time::SystemTime::now()
+                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
+                .unwrap()
+                .as_nanos()
+        ));
+        fs::create_dir_all(path.join("snapback")).unwrap();
+        fs::write(path.join("snapback/schema.q"), SOURCE).unwrap();
+        Self(path)
+    }
+}
+impl Drop for Temp {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
+    }
+}
+
+fn aggregate_id(store: &Path) -> String {
+    Connection::open(store)
+        .unwrap()
+        .query_row(
+            "SELECT r.id FROM r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t WHERE c.name='totals'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+}
+
+#[test]
+#[ignore = "requires frozen 0.4.28 binary via SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN"]
+fn a_0_4_28_store_rebuilds_legacy_aggregate_ids_and_fences_old_devices() {
+    let baseline = PathBuf::from(
+        std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN")
+            .expect("set SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN to the frozen 0.4.28 snapback4 binary"),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        baseline.is_file(),
+        "SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN is not a file: {}",
+        baseline.display()
+    );
+    let version = Command::new(&baseline).arg("--version").output().unwrap();
+    assert!(version.status.success());
+    assert!(
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&version.stdout).contains("0.4.28"),
+        "unexpected baseline: {:?}",
+        version
+    );
+
+    let dir = Temp::new();
+    let group = "x".repeat(200);
+    let args = serde_json::json!({"group": group, "amount": 7}).to_string();
+    let written = Command::new(&baseline)
+        .current_dir(&dir.0)
+        .args(["run", "add", &args, "--as", "alice", "--now", "1", "--json"])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        written.status.success(),
+        "{}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&written.stderr)
+    );
+    let store = dir.0.join(".snapback4/store.sqlite");
+    let legacy = aggregate_id(&store);
+    assert!(
+        legacy.len() > snapback4_core::rows::MAX_ID_BYTES,
+        "the frozen binary must have written the oversized legacy address"
+    );
+    let before: u64 = Connection::open(&store)
+        .unwrap()
+        .query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='generation'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get::<_, String>(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .parse()
+        .unwrap();
+
+    let opened = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_snapback4"))
+        .current_dir(&dir.0)
+        .args([
+            "run",
+            "total",
+            &serde_json::json!({"group": group}).to_string(),
+            "--as",
+            "alice",
+            "--now",
+            "2",
+            "--json",
+        ])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        opened.status.success(),
+        "stdout={} stderr={}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&opened.stdout),
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&opened.stderr)
+    );
+    let answer: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&opened.stdout).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(answer["data"]["value"], 7, "{answer}");
+
+    let digest = aggregate_id(&store);
+    assert_eq!(digest.len(), 64);
+    assert_ne!(digest, legacy);
+    let conn = Connection::open(&store).unwrap();
+    let (after, marker): (u64, String) = (
+        conn.query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='generation'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get::<_, String>(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .parse()
+        .unwrap(),
+        conn.query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key=?1",
+            [snapback4_core::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META],
+            |row| row.get(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap(),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        after > before,
+        "identity adoption must publish a new device generation"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(marker, snapback4_core::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION);
+
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), SOURCE.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let required =
+        snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&bound.schema.public_projection());
+    assert!(
+        required
+            .capabilities
+            .contains(&"maintained-id-sha256-v1".to_owned())
+    );
+    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
+    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
+    old.capabilities
+        .retain(|capability| capability != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");
+    assert!(
+        refusal.message.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"),
+        "{refusal:?}"
+    );
+}

   358	pub fn validate_indexes(tx: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   359	    for (name, table) in &schema.tables {
   360	        let mut checks: Vec<_> = table
   361	            .indexes
   362	            .iter()
   363	            .filter(|(_, i)| i.unique)
   364	            .map(|(name, i)| (name, i.components.len(), 1, true))
   365	            .collect();
   366	        for constraint in &table.constraints {
   367	            if let crate::schema::Constraint::Cap { by, max } = constraint {
   368	                let (index, _) = table
   369	                    .indexes
   370	                    .iter()
   371	                    .find(|(_, i)| i.columns().starts_with(by))
   372	                    .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{name} cap has no index")))?;
   373	                checks.push((index, by.len(), u64::from(*max), false));
   374	            }
   375	        }
   376	        for (index, width, max, nulls_distinct) in checks {
   377	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   378	            let mut previous = None;
   379	            let mut count = 0;
   380	            loop {
   381	                let page = tx.scan(name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256)?;
   382	                if page.is_empty() {
   383	                    break;
   384	                }
   385	                for (_, key) in page {
   386	                    let full = crate::key::decode(&key)
   387	                        .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("invalid activation index".into()))?;
   388	                    let group = full[..width].to_vec();
   389	                    bounds.after = Some(full);
   390	                    if nulls_distinct && group.contains(&Value::Null) {
   391	                        continue;
   392	                    }
   393	                    if previous.as_ref() == Some(&group) {
   394	                        count += 1;
   395	                    } else {
   396	                        previous = Some(group);
   397	                        count = 1;
   398	                    }
   399	                    if count > max {
   400	                        return Err(RuntimeError::Constraint(format!(
   401	                            "cannot activate {name}.{index}: existing group exceeds {max}"
   402	                        )));
   403	                    }
   404	                }
   405	            }
   406	        }
   407	    }
   408	    Ok(())
   409	}

   411	impl super::runner::Runner<'_> {
   412	    /// Authoritative adapters feed an ancestor-ordered batch to the ordinary
   413	    /// insert/update path; captures always resolve inside this transaction.
   414	    pub fn seed_server_rows(
   415	        &mut self,
   416	        rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
   417	    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   418	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   419	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   420	                "server seed requires system authority".into(),
   421	            ));
   422	        }
   423	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
   424	        let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
   425	        rows.sort_by_key(|(n, _)| order.iter().position(|x| x == n));
   426	        let count = rows.len() as u64;
   427	        for (name, row) in rows {
   428	            super::timeline::check_import(self.schema, &name)?;
   429	            // Adoption rewrites are system imports of stored images (LLP 3000.015 §1).
   430	            self.upsert(
   431	                &name,
   432	                &row.field("id")?.clone(),
   433	                row.import_input(&super::ImportInput(())),
   434	            )?;
   435	        }
   436	        self.check_final_exists()?;
   437	        Ok(count)
   438	    }
   439	
   440	    /// A bounded child-first sweep on the common Rows interface.
   441	    pub fn sweep_server_rows(&mut self, limit: usize, expiry_after: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   442	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   443	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   444	                "server sweep requires system authority".into(),
   445	            ));
   446	        }
   447	        let now = self
   448	            .context
   449	            .now
   450	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("sweep clock is not pinned".into()))?;
   451	        let mut count = 0;
   452	        let mut visited = 0;
   453	        for name in self.schema.through_order().into_iter().rev() {
   454	            let Some((index, _)) = self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index() else {
   455	                continue;
   456	            };
   457	            let due = Bounds { gte: Some(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), lte: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() };
   458	            let mut bounds = due.clone();
   459	            bounds.after = expiry_after.get(&name).cloned();
   460	            let mut wrapped = bounds.after.is_none();
   461	            while visited < limit {
   462	                let batch = (limit - visited).min(256);
   463	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, scope| {
   464	                    runner
   465	                        .tx
   466	                        .scan(scope, &name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, batch)
   467	                })?;
   468	                if page.is_empty() {
   469	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   470	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   471	                        bounds = due.clone();
   472	                        wrapped = true;
   473	                        continue;
   474	                    }
   475	                    break;
   476	                }
   477	                let page_len = page.len();
   478	                for (row, key) in page {
   479	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   480	                    if let Some(after) = &bounds.after { expiry_after.insert(name.clone(), after.clone()); }
   481	                    visited += 1;
   482	                    match self.retire_expired_row(&name, &row) {
   483	                        Ok(true) => count += 1,
   484	                        Ok(false) => {},
   485	                        Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED", .. }) => {},
   486	                        Err(error) => return Err(error),
   487	                    }
   488	                }
   489	                if page_len < batch {
   490	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   491	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   492	                        bounds = due.clone();
   493	                        wrapped = true;
   494	                        continue;
   495	                    }
   496	                    break;
   497	                }
   498	            }
   499	        }
   500	        Ok(count)
   501	    }
   502	}

   113	fn ordered_units(table: &Table, rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   114	    let units = |term: &RuleTerm| matches!(term, RuleTerm::Field(f) if matches!(table.columns.get(f), Some(ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. })));
   115	    match rule {
   116	        RuleExpr::Compare(_, l, r) => units(l) || units(r),
   117	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| ordered_units(table, item)),
   118	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered_units(table, inner),
   119	        _ => false,
   120	    }
   121	}

   124	    match rule {
   125	        RuleExpr::Compare(..) => true,
   126	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(ordered),
   127	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered(inner),
   128	        _ => false,

   143	impl Serialize for Schema {
   144	    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
   145	        let required = self.required_capabilities();
   146	        // The derive's field order, omissions and bytes are unchanged for
   147	        // ordinary schemas, including the serialized conformance corpus.
   148	        if required.is_empty() { return Wire::serialize(self, serializer); }
   149	        let mut wire = self.clone();
   150	        for table in wire.tables.values_mut() {
   151	            table.constraints.retain(|c| !matches!(c, Constraint::Recorded));
   152	        }
   153	        let mut carrier = wire.tables.first_entry().ok_or_else(||
   154	            serde::ser::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: required capabilities need a table carrier"))?;
   155	        carrier.get_mut().constraints.push(Constraint::Capabilities(required));
   156	        Wire::serialize(&wire, serializer)
   157	    }
   158	}

   160	impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Schema {
   161	    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
   162	        // The private remote derive uses the ordinary
   163	        // streaming serde codec. No JSON-value or content-buffer replay.
   164	        let mut schema = Wire::deserialize(deserializer)?;
   165	        let mut declared = BTreeSet::new();
   166	        let mut carriers = 0;
   167	        let mut legacy = false;
   168	        for table in schema.tables.values_mut() {
   169	            let mut recorded = 0;
   170	            table.constraints.retain(|constraint| {
   171	                if let Constraint::Capabilities(names) = constraint {
   172	                    carriers += 1;
   173	                    declared.extend(names.iter().cloned());
   174	                    false
   175	                } else if matches!(constraint, Constraint::Recorded) {
   176	                    recorded += 1;
   177	                    false
   178	                } else { true }
   179	            });
   180	            if recorded > 1 || (recorded != 0 && table.recorded.is_empty()) {
   181	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: invalid legacy Recorded marker"));
   182	            }
   183	            if recorded != 0 { legacy = true; declared.insert("recorded-attribution".into()); }
   184	        }
   185	        for name in &declared {
   186	            if !CAPABILITIES.iter().any(|(known, _)| name == known) {
   187	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: unsupported engine capability {name}; upgrade the engine/device")));
   188	            }
   189	        }
   190	        let mut required = schema.required_capabilities();
   191	        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — RY already serialized the dependency closure.
   192	        // RP stamps every emitted schema so old devices refuse its new prediction
   193	        // facts, but an RP reader must still open RY's kept backend/database.
   194	        // All other capabilities and the carrier shape remain exact.
   195	        let legacy_receipt_prediction = !declared.contains("receipt-derived-prediction-v1")
   196	            && required.remove("receipt-derived-prediction-v1");
   197	        // The price carrier can be absent in an old projection. Missing prices
   198	        // are fenced per program, rather than bricking a kept store.
   199	        for cap in ["source-write-reservations-v1", "source-write-reservations-v2"] {
   200	            if declared.contains(cap) { required.insert(cap.into()); }
   201	            else { required.remove(cap); }
   202	        }
   203	        // Stores written before the digest migration have no carrier for this
   204	        // capability. Admit that persisted schema for server-side rebuilding;
   205	        // its next serialization stamps the capability, so old devices refuse.
   206	        if !declared.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1") {
   207	            required.remove("maintained-id-sha256-v1");
   208	        }
   209	        // Before the shared fence, the binder emitted Recorded on F2 tables
   210	        // even when the same schema also declared timelines. Only that legacy
   211	        // representation infers its full requirements; modern carriers remain
   212	        // exact, including when mixed with a legacy marker.
   213	        if legacy && carriers == 0 {
   214	            // A legacy marker only covers the capabilities that predate the fence.
   215	            // New semantics must never inherit permission from this escape hatch.
   216	            declared = required.iter().filter(|name| matches!(name.as_str(),
   217	                "maintained-column" | "recorded-attribution" | "timeline" | "timeline-v2")).cloned().collect();
   218	        }
   219	        if declared != required || carriers + usize::from(legacy) != usize::from(!required.is_empty()) {
   220	            return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: schema requires {required:?}, but declares {declared:?} in {carriers} carriers")));
   221	        }
   222	        let had_prices = !schema.source_reservations.is_empty();
   223	        schema.prepare_receipt_dependencies();
   224	        // Opening an old blob preserves its wire shape. Complete visible
   225	        // declarations can still price a write on demand; hidden ones cannot.
   226	        if !had_prices { schema.source_reservations.clear(); }
   227	        schema.legacy_receipt_prediction = legacy_receipt_prediction
   228	            || (!declared.contains("source-write-reservations-v1") && !schema.receipts.is_empty());
   229	        Ok(schema)
   230	    }
   231	}

   134	    /// Streams the ids of the live rows referencing `id` through `r` to

   139	    /// start at the live suffix, so an expired backlog is never visited.

   197	    /// The engine's own write of a `set null` reference: no rule, every constraint.
   198	    fn clear_reference(&mut self, table: &str, column: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   199	        let mut new = old.clone();
   200	        if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut new { fields.insert(column.to_owned(), Value::Null); }

   204	            runner.reserve_maintains(table, &runner.schema.tables[table])?;
   205	            runner.replace_authorized(table, old, new, true, &patch, 0)
   206	        });
   207	        self.engine_action = outer;
   208	        result
   209	    }

   211	    /// The engine's own delete of a closure row: no rule, its constraints, its
   212	    /// `read through` children's probe, maintains and partition events.
   213	    fn delete_reached(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   214	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
   215	            runner.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
   216	            let table = &runner.schema.tables[table_name];
   217	            runner.reserve_maintains(table_name, table)?;
   218	            runner.delete_row(table_name, old)
   219	        })
   220	    }

   223	/// Rows a child scan holds per seek: the reservation's transient `4 × row`
   224	/// (LLP 3000.039 §5.1, `Schema::delete_reservation`).
   225	const PAGE: usize = crate::schema::references::REFERENCE_PAGE;
   226	
   227	fn through_reference(r: &Referencing<'_>) -> bool {
   228	    r.table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == r.column)
   229	}
   230	
   231	/// The closure's rows, children before parents: a table goes first when no
   232	/// other reached table must be removed before it (the cascade and `read
   233	/// through` edges are acyclic by `check`), and within a table, later
   234	/// discoveries first.
   235	fn deletion_order(schema: &crate::schema::Schema, reached: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
   236	    let tables: Vec<&str> = {
   237	        let mut seen = Vec::new();
   238	        for (table, _) in reached { if !seen.contains(&table.as_str()) { seen.push(table.as_str()); } }
   239	        seen
   240	    };
   241	    // edges: child table -> the reached tables it must be removed before
   242	    // (its cascade parents and its `read through` parent; LLP 3000.039 §3).
   243	    let mut edges: Vec<(&str, &str)> = Vec::new();
   244	    for &child in &tables {
   245	        for &parent in &tables {
   246	            if child != parent && schema.deletion_precedes(child, parent) { edges.push((child, parent)); }
   247	        }
   248	    }
   249	    let mut order: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
   250	    let mut remaining = tables.clone();
   251	    while !remaining.is_empty() {
   252	        // A table no remaining table references can go now (its referencers are gone).
   253	        let position = remaining.iter().position(|t| !remaining.iter().any(|other| other != t && edges.contains(&(*other, *t))))
   254	            .unwrap_or(remaining.len() - 1);
   255	        order.push(remaining.remove(position));
   256	    }
   257	    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(reached.len());
   258	    for table in order {
   259	        out.extend(reached.iter().rev().filter(|(t, _)| t == table).cloned());
   260	    }
   261	    out
   262	}

    21	    // Cache ordinary group keys once per target/query. Predicates and receipt

    24	    // each returned row still decides independently whether to recount.

    26	    pub(super) fn receipt_maintain_pending(&mut self, m: &Maintain, group: Option<&[Value]>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {

    28	        if !self.receipt_pending_groups.contains_key(&m.target) {
    29	            let fields = if let Some(k) = &m.row_key { vec![k.source_key.clone()] }
    30	                else { m.by.iter().map(|f| m.aliases.get(f).unwrap_or(f).clone()).collect() };

    32	            if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
    33	                let member = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&k.table, std::slice::from_ref(&k.member_key), false)?;
    34	                groups = groups.zip(member).map(|(mut source, member)| { source.extend(member); source });

    36	            self.receipt_pending_groups.insert(m.target.clone(), groups);
    37	        }

    39	            group.map_or(!keys.is_empty(), |group| keys.iter().any(|key| key == group)));

    41	            self.value_source_incomplete = true;
    42	            self.components.note(|frame| frame.pending = true);

    47	    fn receipt_overlay_groups(&self, table: &str, fields: &[String], computed: bool) -> Result<Option<Vec<Vec<Value>>>, RuntimeError> {
    48	        if !self.tx.has_provisional(table)? { return Ok(Some(Vec::new())); }
    49	        if computed || fields.iter().any(|f| self.schema.receipt_dependencies.get(table).is_some_and(|owned| owned.contains(f))) {

    51	        }

    55	    // Recover a read's parent/group from the pinned index. A member point uses
    56	    // one ordinary-key lookup; a scan without the parent stays conservative.
    57	    pub(super) fn receipt_read_group(&mut self, m: &Maintain, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> Result<Option<Vec<Value>>, RuntimeError> {
    58	        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(None); }
    59	        let columns = self.schema.tables[&m.target].indexes[index].columns();
    60	        let pinned = |field: &str| columns.iter().position(|c| c == field).and_then(|i| key.get(i)).cloned();
    61	        if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
    62	            if let Some(parent) = pinned(&k.member_key) { return Ok(Some(vec![parent])); }
    63	            if let Some(id) = pinned("member").or_else(|| pinned("id")) {
    64	                let row = self.metered_scan(|r, scope| r.tx.get(scope, &k.table, id.as_str()?))?;
    65	                return Ok(row.and_then(|row| row.field(&k.member_key).ok().cloned()).map(|v| vec![v]));
    66	            }
    67	            return Ok(None);
    68	        }
    69	        Ok(m.by.iter().map(|f| pinned(f)).collect())
    70	    }

    72	    pub(super) fn maintain(&mut self, source: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    73	        self.receipt_pending_groups.clear();
    74	        // Inserts ordinarily charge their actual aggregate work. A deferred
    75	        // predicate cannot select that work on a device, so use the same public
    76	        // worst-case reservation as update/delete before skipping it. Already
    77	        // prepaid writes must not pay twice.
    78	        if self.device && !self.maintain_prepaid && self.schema.maintains.iter().any(|m|
    79	            m.source == source && m.private.is_none() && m.row_key.is_none() && (self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target) || self.schema.tables[&m.target].sync.is_none())) {
    80	            self.reserve_maintains(source, &self.schema.tables[source])?;
    81	        }
    82	        self.maintain_row_views(source, old, new)?;
    83	        let maintains = self.schema.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.source == source && maintain.row_key.is_none());
    84	        for maintain in maintains {
    85	            if self.defer_receipt_maintain(maintain) || (self.device && self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].sync.is_none()) { continue; }
    86	            let source_bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]);
    87	            let target = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target];
    88	            let bytes = source_bytes.saturating_mul(2).saturating_add(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(target).saturating_mul(16 + 4 * target.indexes.len() as u64));
    89	            let prepaid = self.maintain_prepaid;
    90	            if maintain.private.is_some() && self.column_prepaid { self.maintain_prepaid = true; }
    91	            let result = self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| runner.maintain_one(maintain, old, new));
    92	            self.maintain_prepaid = prepaid;
    93	            result?;
    94	        }
    95	        Ok(())
    96	    }

    98	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — reserve interpreted images, both keys, targets and index buffers before allocation; release transient ownership on every exit.
    99	    pub(super) fn maintain_scratch<T>(&mut self, bytes: u64, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   100	        if self.maintain_prepaid { return work(self); }
   101	        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
   102	        let result = work(self);
   103	        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = self.meter.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(bytes);
   104	        result
   105	    }

   107	    fn maintain_one(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   108	        let table = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
   109	        let mut changes: Vec<(Vec<Value>, i128)> = Vec::new();
   110	        for (image, direction) in [(old, -1), (new, 1)] {
   111	            let Some(image) = image else { continue };
   112	            self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
   113	            let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, table);
   114	            if !maintain.selected(&image) { continue; }
   115	            let key = maintain.source_key(&image);
   116	            let change = delta(maintain, &image, direction)?;
   117	            if let Some(existing) = changes.iter_mut().find(|(k, _)| *k == key) { existing.1 += change; }
   118	            else { changes.push((key, change)); }
   119	        }
   120	        for (key, change) in changes {
   121	            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   122	            if let Some(retiring) = self.retiring.as_mut() {
   123	                let entry = retiring.aggregates.entry((maintain.target.clone(), canonical_json(&key))).or_insert_with(|| (key, 0));
   124	                entry.1 = entry.1.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?;
   125	                continue;
   126	            }
   127	            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
   128	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
   129	            }
   130	        }
   131	        Ok(())
   132	    }

   134	    /// Apply a retirement's net aggregate changes, one per target row, in
   135	    /// key order. Only a total the commit really ends with can overflow.
   136	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   137	    pub(super) fn apply_retired_aggregates(&mut self, changes: BTreeMap<(String, String), (Vec<Value>, i128)>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

   142	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
   143	            }
   144	        }
   145	        Ok(())
   146	    }

   149	    pub(crate) fn rebuild_maintain_reported(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, report: &mut crate::store::adoption_report::AdoptionReport) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   150	        let started = std::time::Instant::now();

   152	        self.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;

   158	    /// Build one aggregate from the rows in the store: the target's rows go,
   159	    /// then every source row contributes once. A schema change that adds or
   160	    /// redefines a `maintain` calls this, so a count over existing rows is
   161	    /// right from its first read (day two, LLP 2000.000 §11.2).
   162	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   163	    pub(crate) fn rebuild_maintain(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   164	        let heap = self.meter.used.heap_bytes;
   165	        let saved = self.column_rebuild;
   166	        self.column_rebuild |= maintain.private.is_some();
   167	        let result = self.rebuild_maintain_inner(maintain);
   168	        self.column_rebuild = saved;
   169	        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = heap;
   170	        result
   171	    }
   172	
   173	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   174	    fn rebuild_maintain_inner(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   175	        if maintain.row_key.is_some() { return self.rebuild_row_view(maintain); }
   176	        let target = self.schema.table(&maintain.target).expect("validated");
   177	        let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   178	        let target_bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(target).saturating_mul(16 + 4 * target.indexes.len() as u64);
   179	        self.meter.heap(target_bytes.saturating_mul(256))?;
   180	        loop {
   181	            let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   182	            if page.is_empty() { break; }
   183	            for (existing, key) in page {
   184	                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   185	                self.refuse_timeline_write(&maintain.target, crate::schema::Effect::Delete)?;
   186	                let entries = self.tx.delete(&maintain.target, target, &existing)?;
   187	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   188	                self.row_changed(&maintain.target, Some(&existing), None, Origin::Maintained)?;
   189	            }
   190	        }
   191	        let source = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
   192	        self.meter.heap(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(source).saturating_mul(256))?;
   193	        let mut totals: BTreeMap<String, (Vec<Value>, i128)> = BTreeMap::new();
   194	        bounds = Bounds::default();
   195	        loop {
   196	            let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.source, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   197	            if page.is_empty() { break; }
   198	            for (mut image, key) in page {
   199	                self.rebuilt_source_rows += 1;
   200	                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   201	                materialize_optional_fields(&mut image, source);
   202	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   203	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
   204	                if !maintain.selected(&image) { continue; }
   205	                // @ref LLP 3000.028#6 — a total unique owner key has one contribution; backfill streams bounded pages instead of retaining all lifetime keys in a totals map.
   206	                if maintain.own_keys.is_some() {
   207	                    let heap = self.meter.used.heap_bytes;
   208	                    self.meter.heap(target_bytes)?;
   209	                    self.apply_aggregate(maintain, maintain.source_key(&image), 1, Some(true))?;
   210	                    self.meter.used.heap_bytes = heap;
   211	                    continue;
   212	                }
   213	                self.meter.heap(target_bytes)?;
   214	                let key = maintain.source_key(&image);
   215	                let change = delta(maintain, &image, 1)?;
   216	                let entry = match totals.entry(canonical_json(&key)) {
   217	                    std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Occupied(entry) => {
   218	                        self.meter.used.heap_bytes -= target_bytes;
   219	                        entry.into_mut()
   220	                    }
   221	                    std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Vacant(entry) => entry.insert((key, 0)),
   222	                };
   223	                entry.1 = entry.1.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?;
   224	            }
   225	        }
   226	        for (_, (key, change)) in totals {
   227	            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
   228	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, Some(true))?;
   229	            }
   230	        }
   231	        Ok(())
   232	    }

   234	    fn live_sum(&self, maintain: &Maintain) -> bool {
   235	        matches!(maintain.kind, MaintainKind::Sum { .. }) && self.schema.table(&maintain.source).is_some_and(|source| source.is_expiring())
   236	    }

   238	    /// A zero sum is still a group while source rows remain: one signed
   239	    /// contribution may expire before the other. Keep its candidate row so
   240	    /// a scan, snapshot and offline replica can discover the later live sum.
   241	    fn aggregate_source_present(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   242	        // One returned source image and its encoded key (MemoryRows also materializes count_prefix).
   243	        let bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]).saturating_mul(2);
   244	        self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| {
   245	            let source = &runner.schema.tables[&maintain.source];
   246	            let index = maintain.contribution_index();
   247	            if !source.indexes.contains_key(&index) { return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("maintain {} needs its contribution index", maintain.target))); }
   248	            runner.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   249	            let present = runner.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.count_prefix(allowance, &maintain.source, &index, key, 1))? != 0;
   250	            // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — a local positive witness keeps zero; absence needs complete, currently held source coverage.
   251	            if !present && runner.device && !runner.aggregate_source_complete(maintain, key)? {
   252	                runner.unknown_fact(&maintain.source, &index, key, "zero-sum occupancy");
   253	                return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("the zero-sum group's source occupancy is not known locally; queued without a predicted row".into()));
   254	            }
   255	            Ok(present)
   256	        })
   257	    }
   258	
   259	    fn aggregate_source_complete(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   260	        let source = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.source];
   261	        if source.sync.as_ref().is_none_or(|sync| sync.horizon.is_some()) || self.schema.maintain_subset_unknown(&maintain.target) { return Ok(false); }
   262	        // The target has the same bare audience keys, but no source horizon.
   263	        if !self.upsert_absence_proven(&maintain.target, "byGroup", key)? { return Ok(false); }
   264	        for (name, index) in &source.indexes {
   265	            let values = index.columns().iter().map_while(|column| maintain.by.iter().position(|field| field == column).map(|n| key[n].clone())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
   266	            if self.retained_group(&maintain.source, name, &values)? { return Ok(false); }
   267	        }
   268	        Ok(true)
   269	    }
   270	
   271	    fn apply_aggregate(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: Vec<Value>, change: i128, source_present: Option<bool>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   272	        if self.schema.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.owns(&maintain.target)) {
   273	            return Err(super::timeline::refusal("E_TIMELINE_OWNED", "timeline-owned tables cannot be aggregate targets; maintain a mapped application table instead"));
   274	        }
   275	        let id = maintained_id(&key);
   276	        let target = self.schema.table(&maintain.target).expect("validated");
   277	        self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   278	        let existing = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, &maintain.target, &id))?;
   279	        if self.device && existing.is_none() && !self.upsert_absence_proven(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &key)? {
   280	            self.unknown_fact(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &key, "aggregate base");
   281	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("the affected aggregate value or its absence is not known locally; queued without a predicted row".into()));
   282	        }
   283	        let old_value = existing.as_ref().and_then(|row| row.field("value").ok()).map(Value::as_int).transpose()?.unwrap_or(0);
   284	        let next = i128::from(old_value) + change;
   285	        if !(I53_MIN as i128..=I53_MAX as i128).contains(&next) {
   286	            return Err(aggregate_overflow(maintain));
   287	        }
   288	        let keep_zero = next == 0 && self.live_sum(maintain) && match source_present {
   289	            Some(present) => present,
   290	            None => self.aggregate_source_present(maintain, &key)?,
   291	        };
   292	        if next == 0 && !keep_zero {
   293	            if let Some(existing) = existing {
   294	                self.refuse_timeline_write(&maintain.target, crate::schema::Effect::Delete)?;
   295	                let entries = self.tx.delete(&maintain.target, target, &existing)?;
   296	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   297	                self.row_changed(&maintain.target, Some(&existing), None, Origin::Maintained)?;
   298	            }
   299	            self.mirror_column(maintain, &key, 0)?;
   300	            return Ok(());
   301	        }
   302	        let mut row = crate::small_map::collect([("id".to_owned(), Value::Id(id.clone())), ("value".to_owned(), Value::Int(next as i64))]);
   303	        for (field, value) in maintain.group_fields().iter().zip(key.iter().cloned()) {
   304	            row.insert(field.clone(), value);
   305	        }
   306	        let row = Value::Row(row.into());
   307	        if existing.as_ref() == Some(&row) { return Ok(()); }
   308	        let entries = self.tx.put(&maintain.target, target, &row, existing.as_ref())?;
   309	        self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   310	        self.row_changed(&maintain.target, existing.as_ref(), Some(&row), Origin::Maintained)?;
   311	        self.mirror_column(maintain, &key, next as i64)
   312	    }
   313	}
   314	
   315	pub(super) fn delta(maintain: &Maintain, source: &Value, direction: i64) -> Result<i128, RuntimeError> {
   316	    Ok(match &maintain.kind {
   317	        MaintainKind::Count => i128::from(direction),
   318	        MaintainKind::Sum { of } => i128::from(direction).checked_mul(i128::from(source.field(of)?.as_int()?)).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?,
   319	    })
   320	}
   321	
   322	// @ref LLP 3000.007#17 — an internal sum names its maintain and column, never a retained contribution or computed value.
   323	pub(super) fn aggregate_overflow(maintain: &Maintain) -> RuntimeError {
   324	    RuntimeError::AggregateOverflow { maintain: maintain.private.as_ref().map_or_else(|| maintain.target.clone(), |o|o.table.clone()), column: maintain.private.as_ref().map_or_else(|| "value".into(), |o|o.column.clone()) }
   325	}

   471	    /// At a program commit's end, retire every synced row the commit changed
   472	    /// and every row it inserted whose lifetime has already ended: its final
   473	    /// image was never live at a commit boundary, so it leaves no row for a
   474	    /// later sweep to announce. Inside the commit the
   475	    /// row existed as written (an insert-then-update still works). Engine
   476	    /// bookkeeping, unmetered: the device's prediction does not do it, and
   477	    /// the program's metering is already recorded. Its work, returned, stays
   478	    /// linear in the rows retired: each aggregate row takes one net change
   479	    /// and each audience key is scanned for a live row once. Seeds and loads
   480	    /// keep their rows for the sweep.
   481	    // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — a row whose lifetime ended by its own commit's end never exists at a commit boundary.
   482	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   483	    pub(crate) fn retire_expired_births(&mut self) -> Result<crate::meter::Metered, RuntimeError> {
   484	        let Some(now) = self.context.now else { return Ok(Default::default());
   485	        };
   486	        // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#3 — an expired final image never grants a new recipient the row's id.
   487	        // A row that existed before the commit and ends it already expired is
   488	        // retired too: accounted from the partitions it was in at the commit's
   489	        // start, it revokes there and announces nothing to a partition it only
   490	        // entered with its expiring image.
   491	        let mut changed: Vec<(String, String)> = self.born_rows.keys()
   492	            .chain(self.touched_rows.keys())
   493	            .filter(|(table, _)| self.schema.table(table).is_some_and(|t| t.is_expiring()))
   494	            .cloned().collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>().into_iter().collect();
   495	        if changed.is_empty() {
   496	            return Ok(Default::default());
   497	        }
   498	        // The log's order must not depend on a map's iteration order.
   499	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
   500	        changed.sort_by_key(|(name,id)| {
   501	            (std::cmp::Reverse(order.iter().position(|n| n == name)),id.clone(),
   502	            )
   503	        });
   504	        let meter = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, crate::meter::Meter::new(crate::meter::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort));
   505	        self.retiring = Some(Default::default());
   506	        let retired = changed.iter().try_for_each(|(table_name, id)| {
   507	            let Some(row) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))? else { return Ok(());
   508	            };
   509	            let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   510	            if table.expired(&row, now) { self.retire_expired_row(table_name, &row).map(|_| ()) } else { Ok(()) }
   511	        });
   512	        let aggregates = self.retiring.take().map(|retiring| retiring.aggregates).unwrap_or_default();
   513	        let retired = retired.and_then(|()| self.apply_retired_aggregates(aggregates));
   514	        let work = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, meter).used;
   515	        retired.map(|()| work)
   516	    }

   521	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — omitted defaults use the clock and viewer of the host running the insert.

The integrity claim is therefore precise and modest: **when a delete of row
`p` executes, every live row that references `p` at that moment through a
`restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` reference is refused for, deleted, or
cleared.** It is not "no dangling reference ever exists": a later statement,
even in the same mutation, may insert a row naming `p`, and a `keep`
reference, an excluded reference kind (§2.1) or an expired parent still
leaves the referencing row in place.

## 2. The form

```
column: <table> [?] [on delete restrict | on delete cascade | on delete set null | on delete keep] [default …] [written by …]
```

`on delete` follows the type (and its `?`). One spelling; no `on update`
(ids are immutable).

### 2.1 Which references carry an action

A reference **carries an action** when both ends are ordinary durable
tables: the child (the table declaring the column) and the parent (the
table it names) are neither ephemeral nor engine-owned (maintained views,
private maintained state, timeline-owned tables, and a receipt family's
scope, members and runs tables). Every reference that carries an action has
one: the declared one, or `restrict`.

A reference that does not carry an action keeps today's meaning (the row
stays) and declaring `on delete` on it is `E_REFERENCE_ACTION`:

| Child or parent | Why no action |
|---|---|
| ephemeral child or parent | ephemeral rows live for seconds and are retired by the engine on its own clock; probing or cascading them would make durable deletes depend on presence |
| engine-owned child or parent | the engine derives or orders these rows; no program writes or deletes them on its own (a receipt scope is deletable only by the system) |
| a field-owned column (`written by`) | its value belongs to its writers' audience, not to the table's rules; probing, clearing or cascading through it would disclose or write a field only its owner may (LLP 3000.007's field authority), so the binder gives it no reference index |

The integrity of §1 and the migration of §8 therefore cover every reference
**that carries an action**. A field-owned reference keeps today's meaning,
as a reference into an ephemeral table does: it may name a deleted row, and a
read must treat its target as possibly absent.

### 2.2 Eligibility of each action

| Action | Requires | Refused |
|---|---|---|
| `restrict` | nothing | — |
| `keep` | nothing | — (no index, no probe, no read gate) |
| `cascade` | `cap N by <column>` on the child (exactly that column), or a plain single-column `unique <column>` key (an inferred effective bound of one) | without either bound: `E_CASCADE_BOUND`. A composite unique key does not bound one reference group. With `E_REFERENCE_ACTION`: a cycle in the cascade graph, including a self-reference, or in the union of cascade and `read through` edges (§3 step 6); a child that is `append only`, has any field-owned (`written by`) column, has a derived synced destination that delivers private fields to their owners, feeds a maintained `sum` (view or column), plays any role in a timeline (owned, mapped or authors), is a row-keyed view's member table (its writes may recount a group outside any fixed price), or whose source writes have no fixed price (a `server_only` reservation plan, LLP 3000.022 §14.3); a `read through` reference whose child can carry a finite effective deadline (§6.1). |
| `set null` | an optional (`?`) reference; either `cap N by <column>` or the same single-column unique inference, whose effective bound is one | everything refused for `cascade` except the cycle rule (set null does not recurse), and a column that **carries authority or meaning anywhere in the schema**: `immutable`, `written by`, a `sequence` parent, the root of a recorded or maintained path (`.column.field`), read by **any** rule of **any** table — the child's own read and write rules (directly or as the first hop of `.column.field`), every other table's `exists`/`created` probe that keys or equates on it, and every rule's hop that passes through it (`.task.column`) — named by the child's `sync` audience or horizon index, or named by any `cap` other than `cap N by <column>` alone. (Another table's sync audience can depend on the column only through a `read through` capture of the child's read rule, which the read-rule exclusion already covers.) |

Rationale for the `set null` exclusions: each one is a place where the
column's value is more than "which parent this row has". Clearing a column a
rule reads can grant or remove authority (`update <- .assignee = null`, or
another table's `exists grants[document = .id, folder = null]`), and the
parent's deleter was never authorized to change anybody's authority. An
immutable or field-owned column promises nobody else writes it. A recorded
or maintained path stores a fact resolved through the reference. A sync
audience or horizon would move the row between partitions. What remains is
the column that only says where a row is filed (a category, a folder used for
display, a "related to"). A reference the author's rules read chooses
`cascade`, `restrict` or `keep` instead. A self-reference may be `set null`;
it does not recurse.

**A cap on a `set null` column does not count null.** `cap N by category`
bounds each category's rows; rows whose `category` is null belong to no
parent and are not a group. This is new semantics only for a column that
declares `set null` (a cap on any other nullable column keeps counting its
null group as today), and it is what makes the cap a bound on the
reference's children rather than a limit that the set-null writes would
themselves overflow. Because the null group is then unbounded, **such a cap
never proves a population bound** (a loop's bound, a page's completeness,
mutation admission): those proofs ignore it, as they ignore an index that is
not unique. (A proof that the pinned value is non-null could recover the bound
for one parent's group; §10 records it.) Cap enforcement, activation's group validation, and a device's
cap proofs skip the null group of that column; changing the action away from
`set null` re-validates the cap at activation, null group included.

The unique inference has the same per-parent scope. It applies to required
and optional references: a plain unique reference has at most one row for each
non-null parent id. An optional unique reference may still have an unbounded
null group. Referential actions probe only a concrete non-null parent id, so
that null group is never counted in the action reservation and the inference
never proves a table population bound. When both declarations exist, the
effective bound is the smaller of the explicit cap and one.

### 2.3 The reference index

Every reference whose action probes or writes its children is probed by its
column. The binder reuses a plain index whose leading columns are the
reference (then, for an expiring child, its **effective** deadline column: a
`read through` child's captured `$deadline`, which is the earlier of its own
and its parents' deadlines, else its `expire at` column); otherwise it
synthesizes an engine-named one: `[column, id]`, or
`[column, deadlineColumn, id]` for an expiring child, so one seek skips
an expired backlog (as `read through`'s child index does, LLP 3000.014 §6):
the live rows are exactly `[id, null]` (never expires) and `[id]` with the
deadline after now, so both seeks start at the live suffix and no expired row
is ever visited.
A `read through` reference uses its existing child index. The same index
serves `cap N by <column>`. A `keep` reference gets none.

## 3. What a delete does

A delete of row `p` of table `P` — `delete P[id]`, `delete row`, a unique-key
`delete P[key = …]`, a job, `POST /seed`'s delete, or `snapback4 data` —
runs these steps in the deleting transaction, on every host:

1. **Find and authorize `p`**, as today, with one addition: when any

   gets the ordinary hidden-target refusal. This is LLP 3000.014 §3.1's
   rule, generalized from `read through` children to every referenced table,
   and it keeps step 3 from probing a hidden row's children. The system
   principal passes both rules, as it does every rule.
2. **Reserve.** Charge the reservation `R(P)` of §5.1 on every meter, draw
   its row count from the request's physical authorization allowance, and

/// The target table's columns a content row's `prefix` columns are matched
/// against. `.id` on the content table matches the target's reference to
/// the content table; any other column matches the target's same-named
/// column of the same type, else its sole reference to the same table.
pub fn target_prefix_columns(content_name: &str, content: &Table, target: &Table, prefix: &[String], principal: &str) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for column in prefix {
        let kind = if column == "id" { ColumnType::Ref { table: content_name.to_owned() } } else { content.columns.get(column)?.required().clone() };
        let same_name = target.columns.get(column).filter(|target_kind| column != "id" && target_kind.required() == &kind && column != principal);
        if same_name.is_some() {
            out.push(column.clone());
            continue;
        }
        let by_reference: Vec<&String> = target.columns.iter().filter(|(name, target_kind)| name.as_str() != "id" && name.as_str() != principal && matches!(&kind, ColumnType::Ref { .. }) && target_kind.required() == &kind).map(|(name, _)| name).collect();
        match by_reference.as_slice() {
            [one] => out.push((*one).clone()),
            _ => return None,
        }
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// The proof behind `sync to target[.prefix] by .principal`: the read
/// rule's probe of the target and the target index that probe uses. The
/// partition log delivers by exactly this index; it never reconstructs the
/// mapping from column names or types (a same-typed second reference would
/// deliver one group under the authority of another).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AudienceBinding {
    /// The unique target index `columns ++ [principal]`: a group's principals.
    pub group_index: String,
    /// The target's columns the content row's prefix maps to, in order.
    pub columns: Vec<String>,
    /// The target's principal column, at the probe's `viewer` position.
    pub principal: String,
    /// A target index leading with `principal ++ columns`: a principal's groups.
    pub principal_index: String,
}

pub fn audience_binding(schema: &Schema, table_name: &str, table: &Table, sync: &Sync) -> Result<AudienceBinding, String> {
    let Audience::Target { table: target_name, prefix, principal } = &sync.audience else {
        return Err(format!("{table_name} does not sync to a target table"));
    };
    let target = schema.table(target_name).ok_or_else(|| format!("sync to {target_name} names an unknown table"))?;
    let spelled_prefix = prefix.iter().map(|c| format!(".{c}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
    let mut want = prefix.iter().map(|column| RuleTerm::Field(column.clone())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    want.push(RuleTerm::Viewer);
    let spelled_want = want.iter().map(|t| match t { RuleTerm::Field(f) => format!(".{f}"), _ => "viewer".into() }).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
    let audience_rule = table.rules.read.sync_audience_rule(table_name, table);
    let columns = if audience_rule.is_uniformly_readable() {
        // A public table may sync to any audience; the mapping is by name and type.
        target_prefix_columns(table_name, table, target, prefix, principal).ok_or_else(|| format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}]: {target_name} has no column matching {} (same name and type, or one reference to the same table)", prefix.iter().map(|c| format!("{table_name}.{c}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")))?
    } else {
        // The rule is exactly the probe the sync inverts: a second disjunct
        // would admit viewers the partition never delivers to; a conjunct
        // or a literal in the key would deliver rows the rule denies.
        let exact = format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}] is only sound when the read rule is exactly `exists {target_name}[{spelled_want}]`; it reads under `{}`", table.rules.read.quarry());
        // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#2.2 — a union's group arm inverts its own whole disjunct.
        let probe = if sync.is_union() {
            audience_rule.disjuncts().into_iter().find(|disjunct| matches!(disjunct, RuleExpr::Exists { .. })).ok_or_else(|| exact.clone())?
        } else { audience_rule.as_ref() };
        let RuleExpr::Exists { table: probed, index, key, equalities, .. } = probe else { return Err(exact) };
        if probed != target_name || *key != want || !equalities.is_empty() {
            return Err(exact);
        }
        let index_def = target.index(index).ok_or_else(|| format!("the read rule probes unknown index {target_name}.{index}"))?;
        let index_columns = index_def.columns();
        if !index_def.is_plain() || index_columns.len() != want.len() {
            return Err(format!("the read rule's probe uses {target_name}.{index}, which does not cover exactly `{spelled_want}`"));
        }
        let probe_principal = &index_columns[prefix.len()];
        if probe_principal != principal {
            return Err(format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}] by .{principal} reads recipients from {target_name}.{principal}, but the read rule binds viewer to {target_name}.{probe_principal}; say `by .{probe_principal}`"));
        }
        index_columns[..prefix.len()].to_vec()
    };
    for column in prefix {
        if table.columns.get(column).is_some_and(ColumnType::is_optional) && !table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.fields.contains_key(column)) {
            return Err(format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}] needs required group keys; {table_name}.{column} is optional. Make every content group column required so online rules and device partitions name the same group"));
        }
    }
    for column in &columns {
        if target.columns.get(column).is_some_and(ColumnType::is_optional) {
            return Err(format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}] needs required group keys; {target_name}.{column} is optional. Make every audience group column required so membership discovery, revocation and content delivery name the same group"));
        }
    }
    let mut by_group = columns.clone();
    by_group.push(principal.clone());
    let (group_index, group_def) = target.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| index.is_plain() && index.columns() == by_group).ok_or_else(|| format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}] needs an index on {target_name} over {}", by_group.join(", ")))?;
    if !group_def.unique {
        return Err(format!("the audience index {target_name}.{group_index} must be unique: with two rows for one group and principal, deleting one would revoke a group the other still grants"));
    }
    let mut by_principal = vec![principal.clone()];
    by_principal.extend(columns.iter().cloned());
    let principal_index = target.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| index.is_plain() && index.columns().starts_with(&by_principal)).map(|(name, _)| name.clone()).ok_or_else(|| format!("sync to {target_name}[{spelled_prefix}] needs an index on {target_name} whose leading columns are {} so a device can find its groups", by_principal.join(", ")))?;
    Ok(AudienceBinding { group_index: group_index.clone(), columns, principal: principal.clone(), principal_index })
}

/// The maintained target's row address for a source image: the `by` values.
pub fn maintained_key(source: &Value, by: &[String]) -> Vec<Value> {
    by.iter().map(|field| source.field(field).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)).collect()
}

/// The id of a maintained row is its group's canonical form, as Snapback 2
/// spelled it: an aggregate's identity is its key, and the conformance
/// corpus holds it to this spelling. Programs read aggregates by group,
/// never by id.
pub fn maintained_id(key: &[Value]) -> String {
    crate::value::canonical_json(&key)
}

/// Whether a value is (or contains) the reserved system principal.
pub fn contains_system_principal(value: &Value) -> bool {
    match value {
        Value::Id(id) => id == crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL,
        Value::Array(items) => items.iter().any(contains_system_principal),
        Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => fields.values().any(contains_system_principal),
        _ => false,
    }
}

     3	/-!
     4	# Writes: rule checks and refusals
     5	
     6	From the rules card, `why E_RULE`, `why NOT_FOUND`, `why E_CONFLICT` and the
     7	writes card:
     8	
     9	* **insert** — the insert rule judges the new image (`E_RULE`); a clash on
    10	  `id` or a declared unique key with a hidden row is `E_RULE`; with a visible
    11	  row, `if absent` returns null and an ordinary insert refuses `E_CONSTRAINT`
    12	  or the key's `else CODE`.
    13	* **update** — "readable" means the read rule admits the old row before the
    14	  write; the update rule judges old and next. Denial is `E_RULE` on a readable
    15	  target and `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable one; a missing target is
    16	  `NOT_FOUND`; an `if` condition on an unreadable target is `NOT_FOUND`, and a
    17	  false one on a readable target `E_CONFLICT`; a secondary unique clash is
    18	  `NOT_FOUND` (unreadable target), `E_RULE` (hidden colliding row) or
    19	  `E_CONSTRAINT`. An admitted update may change a hidden row; the result is
    20	  the row if it is readable afterwards, else null.
    21	* **upsert** — patches an existing target as an update; inserts an absent
    22	  one, where an incomplete image or insert-rule denial is `NOT_FOUND`.
    23	* **delete** — `NOT_FOUND` for a missing or unreadable refused target,
    24	  `E_RULE` for a readable one whose delete rule refuses. A row that
    25	  `restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` references name also needs read
    26	  authority (`NOT_FOUND`); then its delete closes over `cascade` references,
    27	  refuses `E_REFERENCED` while a `restrict` reference names a closure row
    28	  from outside the closure, clears `set null` references outside it, and
    29	  removes the closure (LLP 3000.039 §3).
    30	
    31	The order in which checks run when several fail is not documented; the

    42	  | .s x => pure x

    45	def scalarsE (fs : List (String × Value)) : Except Stop (List (String × Scalar)) :=

    48	/-- A column value fits its declaration: only a nullable column takes null. -/
    49	def fits (c : ColDecl) (x : Scalar) : Bool := c.nullable || x != .null

    51	/-- The new image of an insert. An absent nullable column is null; an absent
    52	required column refuses with `missing`. Unknown fields refuse `E_INPUT`. -/
    53	def buildImage (td : TableDecl) (rid : List Nat) (fields : List (String × Scalar))

     8	fn lifetime_changed(schema: &Schema, previous: &Schema, parent: &str) -> bool {
     9	    let old = previous.table(parent);
    10	    let new = schema.table(parent);
    11	    old.and_then(|t| t.expire.as_ref()) != new.and_then(|t| t.expire.as_ref())
    12	        || old.and_then(|t| t.through.as_ref()) != new.and_then(|t| t.through.as_ref())
    13	        || old.into_iter().chain(new).filter_map(|t| t.expire.as_ref()).any(|field|
    14	            crate::successor::interpretation(previous, parent, field) != crate::successor::interpretation(schema, parent, field))
    15	}

    17	pub(super) fn changed_parents(schema: &Schema, previous: Option<&Schema>) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    18	    let mut parents = BTreeSet::new();
    19	    for m in schema.maintains.iter().chain(previous.into_iter().flat_map(|s| &s.maintains)) {
    20	        let Some(owner) = &m.private else { continue };
    21	        if previous.is_none_or(|old| old.table(&owner.table).map(|t| &t.maintained) != schema.table(&owner.table).map(|t| &t.maintained)
    22	            || lifetime_changed(schema, old, &owner.table)
    23	            || schema.maintain_for(&m.target).is_some_and(|next| crate::successor::maintain_rebuild_needed(old, schema, next))) {
    24	            parents.insert(owner.table.clone());
    25	        }
    26	    }
    27	    parents
    28	}

    62	    pub(super) fn mirror_column_pass(&mut self, m: &Maintain) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    63	        let owner = m.private.as_ref().expect("private maintain");
    64	        let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
    65	        loop {
    66	            let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &owner.table, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
    67	            if page.is_empty() { break; }
    68	            for (row, key) in page {
    69	                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
    70	                let group = vec![row.field("id")?.clone()];
    71	                let total = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, &m.target, &maintained_id(&group)))?
    72	                    .and_then(|r| r.field("value").ok().cloned()).unwrap_or(Value::Int(0)).as_int()?;
    73	                // Re-read the current parent in mirror_column: several columns
    74	                // must compose. Missing zero stays physically absent.
    75	                self.mirror_column(m, &group, total)?;
    76	            }
    77	        }
    78	        Ok(())
    79	    }
    80	}

   153	        }
   154	    }
   155	    Ok(computed)
   156	}
