   158	pub(super) fn calendar(name: &str, args: &[Expr], site: &Site) -> Fallible<(i64, i64)> {
   159	    // @ref LLP 3000.040#22-builtins — UTC civil periods take no duration and no offset (time zones are deferred).
   160	    if matches!(name, "month" | "year") {
   161	        if args.len() != 1 { return Err(refusal(site, format!("{name} takes one time and no offset: civil periods are UTC"), format!("{name}(.at)"))); }
   162	        return Ok((0, 0));
   163	    }
   164	    let base = if name == "bucket" { 2 } else { 1 };
   165	    let rewrite = "day(time, 8h), hour(time, 30m), or bucket(time, 1d, 8h); omit the offset for UTC epoch boundaries";
   166	    if args.len() != base && args.len() != base + 1 { return Err(refusal(site, "calendar key takes a time, a bucket duration if needed, and an optional literal offset", rewrite)); }
   167	    let literal = |expr: &Expr| match expr {
   168	        Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Number(n), site } => super::integer_literal(n, site),
   169	        _ => Err(refusal(expr.site(), "calendar durations and offsets must be literals", rewrite)),
   170	    };
   171	    let millis = match name { "day" => 86_400_000, "hour" => 3_600_000, _ => literal(&args[1])? };
   172	    if millis <= 0 { return Err(refusal(site, "bucket duration must be positive", "bucket(.at, 2m)")); }
   173	    let offset = if args.len() > base { literal(&args[base])? } else { 0 };
   174	    if offset < 0 || offset >= millis { return Err(refusal(args[base].site(), "calendar offset must be nonnegative and smaller than its period", rewrite)); }
   175	    Ok((millis, offset))
   176	}
   177	
   178	pub(super) fn predicate(source: &TableInfo, expr: &Expr) -> Fallible<Predicate> {
   179	    match expr {
   180	        Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Bool(b), .. } => Ok(Predicate::Bool(*b)),
   181	        Expr::Member { base, name, .. } if matches!(base.as_ref(), Expr::Focal { .. }) => {
   182	            if source.columns.get(name) == Some(&ScalarType { kind: TypeKind::Bool, optional: false }) { Ok(Predicate::Field(name.clone())) }
   183	            else { Err(refusal(expr.site(), "a bare maintain predicate needs a required boolean column", "compare .column with a scalar literal, or declare column: bool")) }
   184	        }
   185	        Expr::Unary { op, value, .. } if op == "not" => Ok(Predicate::Not(Box::new(predicate(source, value)?))),
   186	        Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "and" || op == "or" => {
   187	            let (a,b) = (Box::new(predicate(source, left)?), Box::new(predicate(source, right)?));
   188	            Ok(if op == "and" { Predicate::And(a,b) } else { Predicate::Or(a,b) })
   189	        }
   190	        Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if matches!(op.as_str(), "=" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=") => {
   191	            let (mut a, mut at) = operand(source, left)?;
   192	            let (mut b, mut bt) = operand(source, right)?;
   193	            coerce(&mut a, &bt, left)?; coerce(&mut b, &at, right)?;
   194	            if matches!(a, Operand::Literal(Value::Id(_))) && bt.required().is_identity() { at = bt.required(); }
   195	            if matches!(b, Operand::Literal(Value::Id(_))) && at.required().is_identity() { bt = at.required(); }
   196	            // @ref LLP 3000.020#3.1 — row-key comparisons preserve total ordering with null below every value.
   197	            if matches!((&a, &b), (Operand::Field(a), Operand::Field(b))
   198	                if a.starts_with("$row.") != b.starts_with("$row.")) {
   199	                at = at.required(); bt = bt.required();
   200	            }
   201	            let scalar = |ty: &Ty| matches!(ty.required(), Ty::Null | Ty::Bool | Ty::Int | Ty::Decimal { .. } | Ty::Money { .. } | Ty::Time | Ty::Text(_) | Ty::Enum(_) | Ty::Id | Ty::Ref(_) | Ty::Principal);
   202	            if !scalar(&at) || !scalar(&bt) || !at.comparable(&bt) || (!matches!(op.as_str(), "=" | "!=") && (at.is_optional() || bt.is_optional() || matches!(at, Ty::Null) || matches!(bt, Ty::Null))) {
   203	                return Err(refusal(expr.site(), format!("maintain comparison needs compatible scalar types; got {} and {}", at.name(), bt.name()), "compare like scalar types; ordered comparisons require non-optional operands"));
   204	            }
   205	            Ok(Predicate::Compare { op: op.clone(), left: a, right: b })
   206	        }
   207	        _ => Err(restricted(expr)),
   208	    }
   209	}
   210	
   211	fn coerce(value: &mut Operand, ty: &Ty, expr: &Expr) -> Fallible<()> {
   212	    if let Operand::Literal(Value::String(s)) = value {
   213	        if ty.required().is_identity() { *value = Operand::Literal(Value::Id(s.clone())); }
   214	        else if let Ty::Enum(variants) = ty.required() {
   215	            if !variants.contains(s) { return Err(refusal(expr.site(), format!("'{s}' is not an allowed variant"), format!("use one of {}", variants.join(", ")))); }
   216	        }
   217	    }
   218	    Ok(())
   219	}
   220	fn operand(source: &TableInfo, expr: &Expr) -> Fallible<(Operand, Ty)> {
   221	    match expr {
   222	        Expr::Member { .. } if path(expr).is_some() => {
   223	            let name = path(expr).unwrap();
   224	            let ty = if name == "id" { Ty::Id } else { source.columns.get(&name).map(Ty::from_scalar).ok_or_else(|| restricted(expr))? };
   225	            Ok((Operand::Field(name.clone()), ty))
   226	        }
   227	        Expr::Literal { value, site } => Ok(match value {
   228	            Literal::Str(s) => (Operand::Literal(Value::String(s.clone())), Ty::Text(s.chars().count() as u32)),
   229	            Literal::Number(n) => (Operand::Literal(Value::Int(super::integer_literal(n, site)?)), Ty::Int),
   230	            Literal::Bool(b) => (Operand::Literal(Value::Bool(*b)), Ty::Bool),
   231	            Literal::Null => (Operand::Literal(Value::Null), Ty::Null),
   232	        }),
   233	        Expr::Unary { op, value, .. } if op == "-" => {
   234	            if let Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Number(n), site } = value.as_ref() { return Ok((Operand::Literal(Value::Int(super::integer_literal(&format!("-{n}"), site)?)), Ty::Int)); }
   235	            Err(restricted(expr))
   236	        }
   237	        _ => Err(restricted(expr)),
   238	    }
   239	}

     4	impl Binder<'_> {
     5	    pub(super) fn planned_view(&mut self, merge: &ast::MergeExpr, out: &mut setup::Body, position: prefix::Position) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
     6	        let site = self.site();
     7	        let cursor = merge.cursor.as_ref().map(|value| self.expr(value, out)).transpose()?;
     8	        if let Some((_, ty)) = &cursor && ty.required() != Ty::Cursor {
     9	            return Err(type_error(&merge.site, "after expects a cursor", "declare c: cursor ? and pass after c"));
    10	        }
    11	        let mut lanes = Vec::new();
    12	        let mut result: Option<BTreeMap<String, Ty>> = None;
    13	        let mut first_site = None;
    14	        let mut field_sources: BTreeMap<String, Vec<(Ty, A)>> = BTreeMap::new();
    15	        // Queries retain the view's shared cursor identity. A non-query with
    16	        // one source is an ordinary admitted scan followed by a row shape;
    17	        // representing it as a merge would reject safe capped mutations.
    18	        let plain = self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Query && merge.lanes.len() == 1
    19	            && merge.lanes[0].project.is_some() && merge.lanes[0].loop_.is_none();
    20	        for lane in &merge.lanes {
    21	            let mut read = *lane.planned.clone().expect("planned lane");
    22	            // @ref LLP 3000.013#2.2 — planning cannot erase point-key admission.
    23	            // Validate the authored predicate in the caller's lexical scope,
    24	            // before binding the proposed lane and its generated selectors.
    25	            if let Some(predicate) = &lane.admission {
    26	                self.clone().row_predicate(&read.table, predicate)?;
    27	            }
    28	            if let Some(range) = &mut read.range { range.cursor = None; }
    29	            self.push_scope();
    30	            let (source, binding) = if let Some((name, domain)) = &lane.loop_ {
    31	                let (source, ty) = self.lane_domain(domain, out)?;
    32	                (Some(source), self.declare(name, ty))
    33	            } else { (None, String::new()) };
    34	            if let Some((_, domain)) = &lane.loop_ {
    35	                self.sources.insert(format!("for/{binding}"), (domain.site().clone(), self.catalog.source.expression(domain)));
    36	            }
    37	            let distinct = lane.distinct.as_ref().map(|value| self.expr(value, out).map(|(value, _)| value)).transpose()?;
    38	            let mut setup = setup::Body::default();
    39	            // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12 — as with authored merges, a lane-dependent
    40	            // residual needs its own selector in eager setup. Deduplication
    41	            // above still reads the original discovery binding.
    42	            if let Some((name, _)) = &lane.loop_
    43	                && read.filter.as_ref().is_some_and(|filter| lanes::filter_uses_lane(filter, name)) {
    44	                let selector = self.temp("selector");
    45	                self.scopes.last_mut().expect("lane scope").get_mut(name).expect("lane binding").runtime = selector.clone();
    46	                setup.push(Stmt::Let { name: selector, value: ir::var(&binding) });
    47	            }
    48	            let (mut scan, _) = self.scan_at(&read, &mut setup, position)?;
    49	            scan.after = cursor.as_ref().map(|(value, _)| Box::new(value.clone()));
    50	            scan.opaque_cursor = cursor.is_some();
    51	            scan.merge_site = Some(site.clone());
    52	            if lane.project.is_none() {
    53	                // Admission was checked against the original domain cap above.
    54	                scan.take = Bound::Literal(merge.take);
    55	                self.pop_scope();
    56	                self.push_value_lane(&mut lanes, lane, MergeLane { guard: None, distinct, branch: lane.branch.clone(), setup: setup.code, scan, source, binding, project: None }, position)?;
    57	                continue;
    58	            }
    59	            scan.after = None;
    60	            let mut conjuncts = Vec::new();
    61	            if let Some(filter) = &read.filter { super::super::intent::split(*filter.clone(), &mut conjuncts); }
    62	            let guard = super::super::intent::conjunction(conjuncts.into_iter().filter(super::super::intent::independent).collect());
    63	            let guard = guard.map(|guard| self.expr(&guard, out).map(|(value, _)| value)).transpose()?;
    64	            let mut projection_setup = setup::Body::default();
    65	            let project_binding = if plain { self.temp("view_row") } else { "$project".into() };
    66	            let (project, ty) = self.shape_object(&project_binding, Ty::Row(read.table.clone()), lane.project.as_ref().expect("view projection"), &lane.site, &mut projection_setup)?;
    67	            if plain {
    68	                scan.merge_site = None;
    69	                scan.after = cursor.as_ref().map(|(value, _)| Box::new(value.clone()));
    70	                let max = scan.take.maximum() as u32;
    71	                let target = self.temp("view_rows");
    72	                out.extend(setup);
    73	                out.push(Stmt::Let { name: target.clone(), value: Expr::Array(Vec::new()) });
    74	                projection_setup.push(Stmt::Push { target: target.clone(), value: project });
    75	                out.push_for(project_binding, LoopDomain::Page(scan), projection_setup);
    76	                self.pop_scope();
    77	                return Ok((ir::var(&target), Ty::Collection(Box::new(ty), max)));
    78	            }
    79	            let fields = match ty { Ty::RowShape(fields) | Ty::RowObject(fields) | Ty::Object(fields) => fields, _ => unreachable!("shape object") };
    80	            if let Some(prior) = &mut result {
    81	                if prior.keys().ne(fields.keys()) {
    82	                    return Err(type_error(&lane.site, format!("view {} branch fields differ from branch at {}", merge.table, first_site.as_ref().unwrap()), "project the same named fields in every view branch").guide("reads"));
    83	                }
    84	                for (name, ty) in fields {
    85	                    let old = &prior[&name];
    86	                    let current = projection_source(lane, &name);
    87	                    let origins = field_sources.get_mut(&name).unwrap();
    88	                    origins.push((ty.clone(), current));
    89	                    old.join(&ty).map_err(|error| self.join_error_many(error.at(&name), origins))?;
    90	                    let joined = view_join(old, &ty).ok_or_else(|| type_error(&lane.site,
    91	                        format!("view {} field {name}: {} conflicts with {} at {}", merge.table, ty.name(), old.name(), first_site.as_ref().unwrap()),
    92	                        format!("project compatible values for {name} in every branch")).guide("reads"))?;
    93	                    prior.insert(name, joined);
    94	                }
    95	            } else {
    96	                first_site = Some(lane.site.clone());
    97	                field_sources = fields.keys().map(|name| (name.clone(), vec![(fields[name].clone(), projection_source(lane, name))])).collect();
    98	                result = Some(fields);
    99	            }
   100	            let project = if projection_setup.is_empty() { project } else { Expr::Block { body: projection_setup.code, value: Box::new(project) } };
   101	            self.pop_scope();
   102	            self.push_value_lane(&mut lanes, lane, MergeLane { guard, distinct, branch: lane.branch.clone(), setup: setup.code, scan, source, binding, project: Some(project) }, position)?;
   103	        }
   104	        if result.is_none() && !lanes.is_empty() {
   105	            let planned = Merge { variant: self.variant(), position: None, view: None, order_keys: Vec::new(), site, lanes };
   106	            // @ref LLP 3000.036.001#3 — the binding check: the runtime's own analysis must agree that every
   107	            // lane is decided (a grant lane by a grant covering the rule) and that the lanes share one
   108	            // position. Otherwise a page with a grant branch reads as written, the grant branch alone.
   109	            if planned.branches() && !snapback4_core::engine::rules::branch_merge_lazy(self.schema, &planned)
   110	                && let Some(read) = merge.lanes.iter().find(|lane| matches!(lane.branch.as_deref(), Some(ir::GRANT_LANE | ir::SYSTEM_LANE))).and_then(|lane| lane.planned.as_deref()) {
   111	                return self.read(read, out);
   112	            }
   113	            return Ok((Expr::Merge(planned), Ty::Page(merge.table.clone(), merge.take)));
   114	        }
   115	        let fields = match self.catalog.view_types.get(&merge.table) {
   116	            Some(Ty::RowShape(fields)) => fields.clone(), _ => result.unwrap_or_default(),
   117	        };
   118	        let mut names = merge.view_order.clone();
   119	        // Keep the projected order aligned with each branch's source scan,
   120	        // including an explicitly ordered id before another field.
   121	        if !names.iter().any(|name| name == "id") { names.push("id".into()); }
   122	        let mut suffix = names.into_iter().map(|name| {
   123	            let kind = fields.get(&name).and_then(cursor_kind).ok_or_else(|| type_error(&merge.site,
   124	                format!("view order .{name} has no scalar column type"), "order by a field projecting a scalar source column in every branch"))?;
   125	            Ok(snapback4_core::cursor::CursorColumn { name, kind })
   126	        }).collect::<Fallible<Vec<_>>>()?;
   127	        suffix.push(snapback4_core::cursor::CursorColumn { name: "$branch".into(), kind: snapback4_core::schema::ColumnType::Text { max: 1024 } });
   128	        let position = ir::ViewPosition { take: merge.take, order: if merge.order == ast::Order::Asc { Order::Asc } else { Order::Desc }, after: cursor.map(|(value, _)| Box::new(value)), suffix };
   129	        self.view_types.insert(merge.table.clone(), Ty::RowShape(fields.clone()));
   130	        Ok((Expr::Merge(Merge { variant: self.variant(), position: Some(position), view: Some(merge.table.clone()), order_keys: merge.view_order.clone(), site, lanes }), Ty::Collection(Box::new(Ty::RowShape(fields)), merge.take)))
   131	    }

   133	    // @ref LLP 3000.013#2.1 — nullable membership is an ordinary filtered lane,
   134	    // below source authorization; no null value is used as an index prefix.
   135	    fn push_value_lane(&mut self, lanes: &mut Vec<MergeLane>, ast: &ast::MergeLane, mut lane: MergeLane, position: prefix::Position) -> Fallible<()> {
   136	        if let Some((_, read)) = &ast.nulls

   145	            // its existing incompleteness latch. Record at most one null lane.

   150	                    Stmt::If { condition: Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Eq, left: Box::new(ir::var(&item)), right: Box::new(ir::lit(Value::Null)) },
# Views: plan, maintain or materialize

**Start here:** Use `view` for derived data: filters and unions plan reads, while counts update in the source transaction. For public post totals, use this excerpt from the complete example below; do not maintain counters in client writes.

```quarry
view postCount: count posts by .author
query total(author: principal):
  return postCount[author]
```

- `E_MAINTAIN_READ_RULE`: grouping lost an authorization field; retain it as a bare key or declare the aggregate's intended read rule.
- `E_QUARRY_SYNTAX`: a view cannot have its own sync line; keep inherited sync or choose `online only` and lose offline coverage.
- `N_MAINTAIN_SYNCED`: the aggregate does not inherit the source horizon; measure it, or choose `online only` only if offline reads and prediction by the named dependent mutations are unnecessary (`predicts` then fails with `E_NOT_PREDICTABLE`).

## Reference

```quarry
table posts:
  author: principal
  body: text <=500
  at: time
  removed: bool default false
  public 'public posts'
  online only
table reposts:
  actor: principal
  post: posts
  at: time
  public 'public reposts'
  online only
view activity:
  posts where not .removed { post: .id, actor: .author, at, repost: false }
  reposts { post, actor, at, repost: true }
query global(c: cursor ?):
  return activity last 20 by .at after c
view postCount: count posts by .author
query total(author: principal):
  return postCount[author]
```

A filter or projection is planned when read. Branches form a union without a copied application table. An aggregate is maintained in the source write's transaction. Public Following is materialized per reader when its source and edge rules admit that disclosure (`guide feeds`).

Each union branch runs under its own source's read rule before filtering or projection. Branches have compatible fields and types. Identity includes both branch and source id; equal ids in different tables remain distinct events. The exposed `id` is the source id. Include a branch discriminator, such as `repost`, when forming a client list key. A predicate on a projected column reaches each source; a constant predicate selects branches. Order fields must map to source columns in every branch.

A maintained view has rows `{ id, <group columns>, value }`. A full group key returns a scalar. An authorized miss is zero; a hidden hit and hidden miss are both null. Pages return existing groups, using `first`/`last`, `by .column`
and `after c`. A domain may use an inherited product cap or the runtime meter.
Source caps can bound distinct groups; no new target cap is enforced.

During adoption, query and sync snapshot reads keep reading the previous backend. A newly added query answers pending until the views are complete. Writes wait, then execute once.
`check` reports N_ADOPTION_PAUSE; dev and deploy print it before activating. Plan the write pause before adopting. Source counts estimate work at measured eb1000 rates; the subtotal is not a floor. The modeled “up to” time is not an SLO or hard bound. Removed or rebuilt rows/indexes add an explicitly unestimated retirement pause, including tables whose names survive. Tables affected by read-through or inherited-expiry changes warn about retirement/recapture: the deletion subset depends on activation time, so their stored populations are not exact deletion counts. On a schema change, an unaffected read-through table separately rewrites every stored row to recompute deadlines; this rewrite count is exact, not a deletion subset. Both pauses remain unestimated. Maintained-column mirrors, cap resets and asset-home retirement also warn when unpriced. Payload width, fanout, cache and WAL/storage affect time.
Activation defaults to a 64 MiB combined main/temp cache target (half each). Set SNAPBACK4_ADOPTION_CACHE_MIB to 0–512; 0 keeps caller settings and larger caller caches are retained. Linux reduces the target for address-space headroom. Workspace is not an RSS cap: the prior 64 MiB main-cache run used about 147 MiB process RSS; sorter RAM follows the cache. SQLite NOMEM after enlargement rolls back and retries once at caller settings; choose 0 for constrained hosts.
The adoption line reports phases, capture fills and rebuilt views with source visits and milliseconds; nested details are included in their parent phase. A failed or interrupted attempt keeps the previous backend; restart retries the complete build.
Signed-in `GET /changes` waits for the whole adoption because reconnecting
requires a durable presence write. That wait grows with the store; it is not
bounded by a rebuild chunk. Query and sync reads have reserved admission capacity
so queued mutations cannot occupy all their request slots.

Omit `read` to derive readability: a public/allow source gives `read <- allow`;
otherwise every field in its read rule must survive as a bare group key, and
that same rule protects the aggregate. Calendar keys and reference paths do
not preserve rule fields. E_MAINTAIN_READ_RULE names missing fields; state an
explicit `read <-` when the aggregate needs its own audience. An explicit
rule always wins. Residency is unchanged: sync is inherited only when all
source audience columns survive as bare keys, without the source horizon;
otherwise the aggregate stays server-only. `online only` opts out.

E_SYNC on a public inherited view names the source, the missing horizon and
the conflicting explicit read. An owner-only read does not make public sync
private. E_QUARRY_SYNTAX refuses a separate sync line on any view. On this public inherited view, remove that
line, then keep the public read (or omit it) for the public offline summary,
or use `online only` and lose offline aggregate/absence coverage. Never narrow
the public source to make the view private. `guide offline-interactions` is
the example and replica census; N_MAINTAIN_SYNCED links it too. For viewer-owned
existence on an eligible public window, that card shows source owner-key
coverage with ordinary `exists` instead of a summary; it does not supply totals.

E_MAINTAIN_READ_EXPIRE means an aggregate over an expiring source has a read
rule that uses fields its group keys do not determine. This includes a source
with an effective deadline inherited through `read through`. Use `read <- deny`
and replace deny with a rule over the group keys, omit `read` to inherit the
source rule, or use `online only` with an explicit key rule. Neither a source
cap nor `online only` permits a value-dependent rule. Non-expiring sources
may authorize their stored value because it is already the live value.

A predicate accepts scalar comparisons, and/or/not, boolean literals and bare
required boolean columns. Equality permits null; ordering requires compatible
non-optional scalars. It cannot read tables, viewer, now, helpers or arithmetic:
store that fact on the source, or use a bounded job. False rows contribute
nothing; updates subtract and add once, coalescing equal groups. Literal
defaults mean the same thing on writes, devices, expiry and adoption.

day(.at), hour(.at) and bucket(.at, 2m) take required time columns.
They also accept an admitted reference path, such as hour(postId.at); a null
recorded time produces the null group. Their int
outputs are floor ordinals from the Unix UTC epoch; day(-1 ms) is -1.
Computed fields are named day, hour and bucket, once each; id and value are
reserved. The same functions work in queries as day(now), hour(now) and
bucket(now, 2m).
The same three functions are table index components over required time columns
at any key position; see `guide indexes` for listings and daily uniqueness.
An optional literal offset anchors the boundary: day(.at, 8h) or
bucket(.at, 1d, 8h) groups 08:00 UTC through just before the next 08:00.
The ordinal is floor((at - offset) / period); offsets are nonnegative whole
durations smaller than the period, including 0ms. hour(.at, 30m) works too.
The same offset belongs in scalar lookups: day(now, 8h). Days remain exactly
86,400,000 ms; no timezone or daylight-saving adjustment is applied. Changing the offset
rebuilds the view without adding a source column.

The following Clique summaries are online-only. Add source sync when its
audience is invertible, and omit the view's online only to inherit it
when every audience column survives as a bare key.

```quarry
table posts:
  authorId: principal
  parentId: posts ?
  at: time
  score: int
  immutable authorId, parentId, at
  public 'posts are public'

//! The catalog: every table (declared or generated for a maintain) with its
//! columns and indexes, plus the named shapes and functions, and where each
//! schema path was declared so a core validation issue can point at a line.

use crate::ast::*;
use crate::diag::{Diagnostic, Site, name_rewrite, unknown};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct TableInfo {
    pub through: Option<snapback4_core::schema::through::Through>,
    pub captures: BTreeMap<String, ScalarType>,
    pub recorded: BTreeMap<String, ScalarType>,
    pub decl: TableDecl,
    pub columns: BTreeMap<String, ScalarType>,
    pub indexes: Vec<IndexDecl>,
    /// Set when the table is a maintain's generated target.
    pub maintained: Option<MaintainDecl>,
}

impl TableInfo {
    pub fn total_unique(&self, index: &IndexDecl) -> bool {
        index.unique && index.is_plain() && index.columns.iter().all(|column| column == "id" || self.columns.get(column).is_some_and(|ty| !ty.optional))
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.013#2.1 — a scan cursor carries declared components only;
    // uniqueness with a nullable component cannot resolve ties between nulls.
    pub fn total_cursor(&self, index: &IndexDecl) -> bool {
        index.columns.iter().any(|column| column == "id") || index.unique && index.words.is_none()
            && index.columns.iter().all(|column| match index.computed.get(column) {
                Some(expr) => super::time_indexes::key(&self.decl.name, &self.columns, column, expr).is_ok(),
                None => self.columns.get(column).is_some_and(|ty| !ty.optional),
            })
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Catalog {
    pub ordinary_searches: Vec<String>,
    pub source: crate::source::SourceMap,
    pub feed_views: BTreeMap<String, super::feed_view::Plan>,
    pub extremum_domains: BTreeMap<String, ReadExpr>,
    pub read_origins: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub canonical_read_origins: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub view_reads: BTreeMap<String, crate::ast::MergeExpr>,
    pub view_types: BTreeMap<String, crate::types::Ty>,
    pub planner_notes: Vec<Diagnostic>,
    /// Exact cap declarations that would admit an otherwise fully verified
    /// owner-or-membership page, keyed by the read's source site.
    pub membership_cap_repairs: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub synthesized: std::collections::BTreeSet<(String, String)>,
    pub documents: Vec<Document>,
    pub tables: BTreeMap<String, TableInfo>,
    pub maintains: BTreeMap<String, MaintainDecl>,
    pub shapes: BTreeMap<String, ShapeDecl>,
    pub functions: BTreeMap<String, FunctionDecl>,
    pub effects: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}

impl Catalog {
    pub fn build(documents: Vec<Document>, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) -> Self {
        let mut tables: BTreeMap<String, TableInfo> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut maintains = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut shapes: BTreeMap<String, ShapeDecl> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut functions: BTreeMap<String, FunctionDecl> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut effects = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut effect_sites: BTreeMap<String, Site> = BTreeMap::new();
        for doc in &documents {
            for table in &doc.tables {
                if tables.contains_key(&table.name) {
                    diagnostics.push(unknown(&table.site, format!("duplicate table {}", table.name), "rename one of the two tables"));
                    continue;
                }
                let mut columns = BTreeMap::new();
                let mut ok = true;
                for column in &table.columns {
                    if column.name == "id" {
                        diagnostics.push(unknown(&column.site, format!("table {} gets id implicitly; remove the id column", table.name), "delete this line"));
                        ok = false;
                        continue;
                    }
                    if columns.insert(column.name.clone(), column.type_.clone()).is_some() {
                        diagnostics.push(unknown(&column.site, format!("duplicate column {}.{}", table.name, column.name), "rename one of the two columns"));
                        ok = false;
                    }
                }
                for field in &table.search {
                    if !matches!(columns.get(field), Some(ScalarType { kind: TypeKind::Text { .. }, .. })) {
                        diagnostics.push(crate::diag::type_error(&table.site, format!("search {} requires a text column on {}", field, table.name), format!("declare `{field}: text <=2000` before `search {field}`")).guide("search"));
                        ok = false;

   228	    /// The declaration site behind a schema validation path.
   229	    pub fn site_for(&self, path: &str) -> Site {
   230	        let mut parts = path.split('.');
   231	        if parts.next() == Some("tables")
   232	            && let Some(table) = parts.next()
   233	            && let Some(info) = self.tables.get(table)
   234	        {
   235	            let rest: Vec<&str> = parts.collect();
   236	            match rest.as_slice() {
   237	                ["columns", column] => {
   238	                    if let Some(c) = info.decl.columns.iter().find(|c| &c.name == column) {
   239	                        return c.site.clone();
   240	                    }
   241	                }
   242	                ["indexes", index] => {
   243	                    if let Some(i) = info.indexes.iter().find(|i| &i.name == index) {
   244	                        return i.site.clone();
   245	                    }
   246	                }
   247	                ["rules", effect] => {
   248	                    let effect = match *effect { "insert-if-absent" | "insert if absent" => "insert", effect => effect };
   249	                    if let Some(r) = info.decl.rules.iter().find(|r| r.effect.word() == effect) {
   250	                        return r.site.clone();
   251	                    }
   252	                }
   253	                ["sync"] => {
   254	                    if let Some(sync) = &info.decl.sync {
   255	                        return sync.site.clone();
   256	                    }
   257	                }
   258	                _ => {}
   259	            }
   260	            return info.decl.site.clone();
   261	        }
   262	        if path.starts_with("maintains[")
   263	            && let Some(position) = path.strip_prefix("maintains[").and_then(|p| p.split(']').next()).and_then(|p| p.parse::<usize>().ok())
   264	            && let Some(maintain) = self.maintains.values().nth(position)
   265	        {
   266	            return maintain.site.clone();
   267	        }
   268	        self.documents.first().map(|d| Site::new(&d.file, 1, 1)).unwrap_or_default()
   269	    }
   270	}

   272	fn int_range_of(ty: &crate::ast::ScalarType) -> Option<(Option<i64>, Option<i64>)> {
   273	    match &ty.kind {
   274	        crate::ast::TypeKind::IntRange { min, max } => Some((*min, *max)),
   275	        crate::ast::TypeKind::List { item, .. } => int_range_of(item),
   276	        _ => None,
   277	    }

   317	/// What one case comes to; `executed` counts engine and model calls.
   318	pub struct Checked {
   319	    pub verdict: Verdict,
   320	    pub executed: u64,
   321	    pub pages: u64,
   322	    pub mutation: bool,
   323	    /// The first outcome's class on an agreeing case (`committed`, a code,

   328	/// The module, or why the case is outside the fragment.
   329	pub fn module(source: &str) -> Result<LeanModule, String> {
   330	    let (document, diagnostics) = snapback4_lang::parse_document("schema.q", source);
   331	    if !diagnostics.is_empty() {
   332	        return Err("parse".into());
   333	    }
   334	    snapback4_lang::emit::lean::from_documents(&[document]).map_err(|u| u.reason)
   335	}

   337	/// Compare one case whose source compiles. `Err` is a harness or emitter
   338	/// defect (never a verdict).
   339	pub fn compare(case: &Case, source: &str) -> Result<Checked, String> {
   340	    let unsupported = |reason: String| Ok(Checked { verdict: Verdict::Unsupported(reason), executed: 0, pages: 0, mutation: false, class: String::new() });
   341	    let module = match module(source) {
   342	        Ok(m) => m,
   343	        Err(reason) => return unsupported(reason),
   344	    };
   345	    let mutation = case.program.mutation();
   346	    if let Err(u) = module.program("run") {
   347	        return unsupported(u.reason);
   348	    }
   349	    if mutation {
   350	        if let Err(u) = module.program("observe") {
   351	            return unsupported(format!("observe-{}", u.reason));
   352	        }
   353	    }
   354	    let store = match module.store(&case.rows) {
   355	        Ok(s) => s,
   356	        Err(u) => return unsupported(u.reason),
   357	    };
   358	    let mut m_args = match module.tag_args("run", &case.args) {
   359	        Ok(a) => a,
   360	        Err(u) => return unsupported(u.reason),
   361	    };
   362	    // The prelude: each step on the engine and on the model's store, in order.
   363	    for i in 0..case.steps.len() {
   364	        if let Err(u) = module.program(&format!("prep{i}")) {
   365	            return unsupported(format!("prelude-{}", u.reason));
   366	        }
   367	        if let Err(u) = module.tag_args(&format!("prep{i}"), &case.steps[i].args) {
   368	            return unsupported(format!("prelude-{}", u.reason));
   369	        }
   370	    }
   371	    let (mut engine, prelude) = execute::world(case, source)?;
   372	    engine.set_ceilings(Ceilings::default());
   373	    let mut executed = 0;
   374	    let mut pages = 0;
   375	    let mut store = store;
   376	    let mut steps = prelude.iter();
   377	    let mut trail = vec![];
   378	    for (i, step) in case.steps.iter().enumerate() {
   379	        let name = format!("prep{i}");
   380	        if step.sweep {
   381	            let e_sweep = steps.next().ok_or("prelude sweep outcome missing")?;
   382	            if e_sweep.kind != "sweep" || e_sweep.value.get("error").is_some() {
   383	                return Err(format!("engine prelude sweep failed: {:?}", e_sweep.value));
   384	            }
   385	            let args = module.tag_args(&name, &step.args).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   386	            let viewer = step.viewer.as_deref().unwrap_or(&case.principal);
   387	            let swept = ask(&module.case_at_sweep(&name, store.clone(), viewer, args, None, step.at, true).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   388	            executed += 1;
   389	            if swept["kind"] != "committed" { return Err(format!("Lean prelude sweep failed: {swept}")); }
   390	            store = swept["store"].clone();
   391	        }
   392	        let e_raw = steps.next().ok_or("prelude outcome missing")?.clone();
   393	        let args = module.tag_args(&name, &step.args).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   394	        let viewer = step.viewer.as_deref().unwrap_or(&case.principal);
   395	        let m_raw = ask(&module.case_at(&name, store.clone(), viewer, args, None, step.at).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   396	        executed += 2;
   397	        let (e, m) = (engine_canon(&e_raw), model_canon(&m_raw));
   398	        trail.push(trail_entry(&e, &m));
   399	        if let Some(f) = differ(&e, &m) {
   400	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding(&format!("prelude-{f}"), &e, &m, e_raw, &m_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   401	        }
   402	        if m.kind == "committed" {
   403	            store = m_raw["store"].clone();
   404	        }
   405	    }
   406	    if case.sweep {
   407	        let e_sweep = steps.next().ok_or("final sweep outcome missing")?;
   408	        if e_sweep.kind != "sweep" || e_sweep.value.get("error").is_some() {
   409	            return Err(format!("engine final sweep failed: {:?}", e_sweep.value));
   410	        }
   411	        let swept = ask(&module.case_at_sweep("run", store.clone(), &case.principal, m_args.clone(), None, case.clock, true).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   412	        executed += 1;
   413	        if swept["kind"] != "committed" { return Err(format!("Lean final sweep failed: {swept}")); }
   414	        store = swept["store"].clone();
   415	    }
   416	    if mutation {
   417	        let e_raw = execute::execute(&mut engine, case, "run", &case.args);
   418	        let m_raw = ask(&module.case_at("run", store.clone(), &case.principal, m_args, None, case.clock).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   419	        executed += 2;
   420	        let (e, m) = (engine_canon(&e_raw), model_canon(&m_raw));
   421	        let first_class = e.class("kind");
   422	        let mut trail = vec![trail_entry(&e, &m)];
   423	        if let Some(f) = differ(&e, &m) {
   424	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding(f, &e, &m, e_raw, &m_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   425	        }
   426	        // The resulting stores, seen through `observe`.
   427	        let after = if m.kind == "committed" { m_raw["store"].clone() } else { store };
   428	        let o_args = module.tag_args("observe", &case.args).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   429	        let eo_raw = execute::execute(&mut engine, case, "observe", &case.args);
   430	        let mo_raw = ask(&module.case_at("observe", after, &case.principal, o_args, None, case.clock).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   431	        executed += 2;
   432	        let (eo, mo) = (engine_canon(&eo_raw), model_canon(&mo_raw));
   433	        trail.push(trail_entry(&eo, &mo));
   434	        if let Some(f) = differ(&eo, &mo) {
   435	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding(&format!("post-{f}"), &eo, &mo, eo_raw, &mo_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });

The cross-table starvation case is confirmed by the committed control flow: with one retained due row in the first table, every `limit = 1` call wraps back to it, leaving later tables unvisited. I’m also checking a mismatch between the new ungrouped migration test and the parser in these commits.

fn title(value: &str) -> String {
    let mut chars = value.chars();
    match chars.next() {
        Some(first) => first.to_uppercase().collect::<String>() + chars.as_str(),
        None => String::new(),
    }
}

/// The columns of a generated maintain target: `id`, `value`, and the `by`
/// columns typed as the source declares them.
pub fn maintain_target(source: &TableInfo, maintain: &MaintainDecl) -> Fallible<TableDecl> {
    let site = maintain.site.clone();
    if source.maintained.is_some() { return Err(super::maintains::refusal(&site, "a maintain cannot use another maintain as its source", "define the view over application source rows, or use a job sweep")); }
    let mut columns = Vec::new();
    let value_type = match &maintain.column {
        None => ScalarType { kind: TypeKind::Int, optional: false },
        Some(column) => match source.columns.get(column) {
            Some(ty) if ty.optional && matches!(ty.kind, TypeKind::Int | TypeKind::IntRange { .. } | TypeKind::Decimal { .. } | TypeKind::Money { .. }) => {
                return Err(type_error(&site, format!("sum over {}.{column} cannot add null: the numeric column is optional (`?`); its numeric range is accepted", maintain.source),
                    format!("make {column} required (`{column}: {}`) and give every row a numeric contribution; if absence must stay distinct, add a required numeric contribution column default 0 and sum that column instead", crate::print::scalar_type(&ty.required()))).guide("maintains"));
            }
            Some(ty) if matches!(ty.kind, TypeKind::IntRange { .. }) => ScalarType { kind: TypeKind::Int, optional: false },
            Some(ty) if matches!(ty.kind, TypeKind::Int | TypeKind::Decimal { .. } | TypeKind::Money { .. }) => ty.required(),
            Some(ty) => return Err(type_error(&site, format!("sum over {}.{column} needs int, decimal or money, not {}", maintain.source, crate::print::scalar_type(ty)), format!("view {}: count {} by {}", maintain.name, maintain.source, maintain.keys.iter().map(|key| super::maintains::bare_key(key).map_or_else(|| crate::print::expression(key), |name| format!(".{name}"))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")))),
            None => return Err(unknown(&site, format!("sum names unknown column {}.{column}", maintain.source), name_rewrite(column, source.columns.keys().map(String::as_str), None))),
        },
    };
    columns.push(ColumnDecl { on_delete: None, sequence: None, written_by: None, readable_by_audience: false, maintained: None, default: None, name: "value".into(), type_: value_type, site: site.clone() });
    let computed = super::maintains::keys(&source, maintain)?;
    let aliases = super::maintains::inherited_aliases(source,maintain);
    if let Some(expr) = &maintain.filter { super::maintains::predicate(&source, expr)?; }
    for field in &maintain.by {
        let ty = if computed.contains_key(field) { ScalarType { kind: TypeKind::Int, optional: computed[field].column.contains('.') } } else { source.columns[aliases.get(field).unwrap_or(field)].clone() };
        columns.push(ColumnDecl { on_delete: None, sequence: None, written_by: None, readable_by_audience: false, maintained: None, default: None, name: field.clone(), type_: ty, site: site.clone() });
    }
    let mut indexes = vec![IndexDecl { name: "byGroup".into(), columns: maintain.by.clone(), unique: true, refusal: None, words: None, computed: BTreeMap::new(), site: site.clone() }];
    let mut names = BTreeSet::from(["byGroup".to_owned(), "byId".to_owned()]);
    for index in &maintain.indexes {
        if !names.insert(index.name.clone()) { return Err(super::maintains::refusal(&index.site, format!("duplicate maintain index {}", index.name), "use a distinct index name; byGroup and byId are generated")); }
        let index = index.clone();
        if index.columns.contains(&"value".into()) {
            // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.21 — stored order is stale; the sound server count upper-bound threshold read is not built.
            if source.decl.expire.is_some() || source.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.expiring) { return Err(Diagnostic::new(&index.site, "E_QUARRY_MAINTAIN_EXPIRE", format!("maintain {} cannot order by value because source {} expires: stored order is stale before the physical sweep, so taking stored top-N can miss a live winner; a count upper-bound threshold scan is not built", maintain.name, maintain.source), "for an entity-time window over a non-expiring source, use the Trending predicate in guide feeds; for expiring contributions, stream each candidate's live count and rank only a complete candidate domain; a meter cut makes the ranking incomplete").guide("feeds")); }
            // @ref LLP 3000.007#14 — ruling 41's interim retires with maintained columns.
            let value_at = index.columns.iter().position(|field| field == "value").unwrap();
            let fields = index.columns.iter().collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
            if !index.is_plain() || fields.len() != index.columns.len()
                || index.columns[value_at..] != ["value", "id"]
                || index.columns[..value_at].iter().any(|field| !maintain.by.contains(field)) {
                return Err(super::maintains::refusal(&index.site,
                    "a maintain value index is a prefix of group fields, then value, id; fields cannot repeat",
                    "end this index with value, id; for post-time ties declare likeCount: count likes on posts, then read posts last 20 by .likeCount, .at after c (guide maintains)"));
            }
        }
        indexes.push(index);
    }
    Ok(TableDecl {
        receipts: None,
        ephemeral: None,
        search: Vec::new(),
        name: maintain.name.clone(),
        columns,
        indexes,
        rules: maintain.read.iter().cloned().collect(),
        immutable: Vec::new(),
        caps: Vec::new(),
        final_exists: Vec::new(),
        retain: None,
        public: None,
        sync: None,
        online_only: maintain.online_only,
        not_before: None,
        expire: None,
        site,
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    #[test]
    fn quarry_refuses_nullable_target_sync_group_keys() {
        let source = r#"
table memberships:
  room: id ?
  principal: principal
  unique byRoomPrincipal: room, principal
  by byPrincipalRoom: principal, room, id
  read <- .principal = viewer
table messages:
  room: id
  body: text <=100
  by byRoom: room, id
  read <- exists memberships[.room, viewer]
  sync to memberships[.room]
"#;
        let refused = crate::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
        assert!(refused.diagnostics.iter().any(|diagnostic| diagnostic.code == "E_SYNC" && diagnostic.guide == "sync" && diagnostic.message.contains("needs required group keys") && diagnostic.rewrite.contains("remove `?`")), "{:?}", refused.diagnostics);
        let accepted = crate::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.replace("room: id ?", "room: id"))]);
        assert!(accepted.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", accepted.diagnostics);
    }

    // LLP 3000.036 §1 A: the rule in source form, the paved split, and no "make it public".
    #[test]
    fn e_sync_quotes_the_source_rule_and_names_the_split() {
        let sync = |rule: &str, sync: &str| {
            let source = format!("table claims:\n  claimant: principal\n  postedBy: principal\n  approved: bool\n  read <- {rule}\n  insert <- .postedBy = viewer\n  {sync}\n");
            let bound = crate::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source)]);
            bound.diagnostics.into_iter().find(|d| d.code == "E_SYNC").expect("E_SYNC")
        };
        // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#2.1 — two parties are a union now; naming one of them is a disagreement whose rewrite is the union.
        let two = sync(".claimant = viewer or .postedBy = viewer", "sync to .claimant");
        assert!(two.message.contains("`read <- .claimant = viewer or .postedBy = viewer`"), "{}", two.message);
        assert!(two.rewrite.contains("`sync to .claimant or .postedBy`"), "{}", two.rewrite);
        let source = "table claims:\n  claimant: principal\n  postedBy: principal\n  read <- .claimant = viewer or .postedBy = viewer\n  insert <- .postedBy = viewer\n  sync\n";
        assert!(crate::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]).diagnostics.is_empty());
        // A disjunct that names no reader is still refused with the split.
        let partial = sync("(.claimant = viewer and .approved) or .postedBy = viewer", "sync");
        assert!(partial.message.contains("do not make private rows public"), "{}", partial.message);
        let shared = sync(".approved or .postedBy = viewer", "sync");
        assert!(shared.message.contains("`read <- .approved or .postedBy = viewer`") && !shared.message.contains("Bool"), "{}", shared.message);
        assert!(shared.rewrite.contains("`public '..'` table") && shared.rewrite.contains("`.postedBy = viewer`"), "{}", shared.rewrite);
        // The split the rewrite names compiles.
        let split = "table claims:\n  claimant: principal\n  postedBy: principal\n  read <- exists claimsParties[.id, viewer]\n  insert <- .postedBy = viewer\n  after insert <- exists claimsParties[item = .id, party = .claimant]\n  after insert <- exists claimsParties[item = .id, party = .postedBy]\n  sync\ntable claimsParties:\n  item: claims\n  party: principal\n  unique item, party\n  immutable item, party\n  read <- exists claimsParties[.item, viewer]\n  insert <- created claims[.item]\n  sync\n";
        let bound = crate::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), split.into())]);
        assert!(bound.diagnostics.iter().all(|d| !d.code.starts_with("E_")), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
    }
}

//! A commit's retirement of the rows it inserted already expired
//! (`Runner::retire_expired_births`).
use super::runner::Runner;
use crate::{Context, Store, Value, meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter}, schema::Schema, value::object};

const SCHEMA: &str = "table members:
  group: text <=10
  person: principal
  until: time ?
  unique byGroupPerson: group, person
  by byExpiry: until
  expire at .until
  read <- .person = viewer
  insert <- exists members[.group, viewer]
  sync to .person
table notes:
  group: text <=10
  by byGroup: group, id
  read <- exists members[.group, viewer]
  insert <- allow
  sync to members[.group]
";

/// Each retirement asks whether its audience key keeps a live row. Removing
/// expired rows cannot change the answer, so the key is scanned once, not
/// once per sibling: the work stays linear in the rows retired.
#[test]
fn retiring_expired_siblings_scans_their_key_once() {
    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), SCHEMA.into())]);
    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
    // The compiler links its own build of this crate: cross by the wire.
    let schema: Schema = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::to_value(&bound.schema).unwrap()).unwrap();
    let mut store = Store::memory().unwrap();
    store.install(&schema).unwrap();
    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
    let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &schema, Context::system().at(150), Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort), 0);
    let n = 200_u64;
    let ids: Vec<String> = (0..n).map(|i| format!("m{i:03}")).collect();
    for id in &ids {
        let row = object([("id", Value::Id(id.clone())), ("group", Value::String("g".into())), ("person", Value::Id("dev:alice".into())), ("until", Value::Int(100))]);
        runner.insert("members", row.import_input(&super::ImportInput(()))).unwrap();
    }
    let work = runner.retire_expired_births().unwrap();
    assert!(work.examined <= 2 * n, "{work:?}");
    assert!(ids.iter().all(|id| tx.get("members", id).unwrap().is_none()));
    assert!(runner.events.take().is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn retired_birth_releases_table_and_group_occupancy_in_memory_rows() {
    use crate::rows::{MemoryRows, Rows};
    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("caps.q".into(), include_str!("../../tests/fixtures/expired-birth-cap.q").into())]);
    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
    let schema: Schema = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::to_value(&bound.schema).unwrap()).unwrap();
    let rows = MemoryRows::new();
    let row = |id: &str, until| object([("id", Value::Id(id.into())), ("group", Value::String("a".into())), ("until", until)]);
    let check = |expected| {
        assert_eq!(rows.cap_count("items", &[], &[]).unwrap(), expected);
        assert_eq!(rows.cap_count("items", &["group".into()], &[Value::String("a".into())]).unwrap(), expected);
    };
    {
        let mut runner = Runner::new(&rows, &schema, Context::system().at(100), Meter::new(Ceilings::default(), Cut::Abort), 0);
        runner.insert("items", row("born", Value::Int(0)).import_input(&super::ImportInput(()))).unwrap();
        check(1); // Capacity is physical, even before this birth is retired.
        runner.retire_expired_births().unwrap();
        assert!(runner.events.take().is_empty());
    }
    check(0);
    assert!(rows.get("items", "born").unwrap().is_none());
    let mut next = Runner::new(&rows, &schema, Context::system().at(100), Meter::new(Ceilings::default(), Cut::Abort), 0);
    next.insert("items", row("live", Value::Null).import_input(&super::ImportInput(()))).unwrap();
    next.retire_expired_births().unwrap();
    check(1);
    assert!(rows.get("items", "live").unwrap().is_some());
}

   186	/// Why [`lean`] produced no module.
   187	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   188	pub enum LeanError {
   189	    /// The sources do not compile; the model takes only checked programs.
   190	    Diagnostics(Vec<String>),
   191	    /// A schema-level construct outside the fragment.
   192	    Unsupported(Unsupported),
   193	}
   194	
   195	/// Check `sources` with [`crate::compile`], then translate their surface
   196	/// trees. A program outside the fragment is recorded per program in
   197	/// [`LeanModule::programs`]; a schema construct outside it refuses the whole
   198	/// module.
   199	pub fn lean(sources: &[(String, String)]) -> Result<LeanModule, LeanError> {
   200	    let bound = crate::compile(sources);
   201	    if !bound.diagnostics.is_empty() {
   202	        return Err(LeanError::Diagnostics(bound.diagnostics.iter().map(|d| format!("{}: {}", d.code, d.message)).collect()));
   203	    }
   204	    let documents: Vec<Document> = sources.iter().map(|(file, source)| crate::parse_document(file, source).0).collect();
   205	    from_documents(&documents).map_err(LeanError::Unsupported)
   206	}
   207	
   208	/// Translate documents that [`crate::compile`] has accepted. Callers that
   209	/// have not checked them must use [`lean`].
   210	pub fn from_documents(documents: &[Document]) -> R<LeanModule> {
   211	    for d in documents {
   212	        for (present, what) in [
   213	            (!d.maintains.is_empty(), "maintain"),
   214	            (!d.timelines.is_empty(), "timeline"),
   215	            (!d.views.is_empty() || !d.feed_views.is_empty(), "view"),
   216	            (!d.effects.is_empty(), "effect"),
   217	            (!d.shapes.is_empty(), "shape"),
   218	            (!d.actions.is_empty(), "action"),
   219	            (!d.routes.is_empty(), "route"),
   220	            (!d.schedules.is_empty(), "schedule"),
   221	            (d.identity.is_some(), "identity"),
   222	        ] {
   223	            if present {
   224	                return no(&format!("declaration-{what}"), format!("a {what} declaration in {}", d.file));
   225	            }
   226	        }
   227	    }
   228	    let decls: Vec<&ast::TableDecl> = documents.iter().flat_map(|d| d.tables.iter()).collect();
   229	    let mut tables = Vec::new();
   230	    for t in &decls {
   231	        tables.push(table_shape(t)?);
   232	    }
   233	    let module_tables = tables.clone();
   234	    let mut schema_tables = Vec::new();
   235	    for (t, shape) in decls.iter().zip(&tables) {
   236	        schema_tables.push(table_json(t, shape, &module_tables)?);
   237	    }
   238	    let functions: Vec<&ast::FunctionDecl> = documents.iter().flat_map(|d| d.functions.iter()).collect();
   239	    let helper_names: Vec<String> = functions.iter().map(|f| f.name.clone()).collect();
   240	    let mut module = LeanModule {
   241	        tables,
   242	        surface_tables: decls.iter().map(|table| (*table).clone()).collect(),
   243	        schema: json!({"tables": schema_tables}),
   244	        helpers: json!([]),
   245	        programs: BTreeMap::new(),
   246	        args: BTreeMap::new(),
   247	    };
   248	    let mut helpers = Vec::new();
   249	    for f in &functions {
   250	        let ast::FunctionBody::Expression(body) = &f.body else {
   251	            return no("helper-block", format!("helper {} has a block body", f.name));
   252	        };
   253	        let mut scope = Scope::new(&module, &helper_names);
   254	        for a in &f.args {
   255	            if a.type_.optional {
   256	                return no("helper-optional-parameter", format!("{}({})", f.name, a.name));
   257	            }
   258	            scope.vars.insert(a.name.clone(), Ty::Scalar(Kind::of(&a.type_.kind)?));
   259	        }
   260	        let body = scope.expr(body)?;
   261	        helpers.push(json!({"name": f.name, "params": f.args.iter().map(|a| a.name.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), "body": body}));
   262	    }
   263	    module.helpers = Json::Array(helpers);
   264	    let programs: Vec<&ast::ProgramDecl> = documents.iter().flat_map(|d| d.programs.iter()).collect();
   265	    let mut signatures = BTreeMap::new();
   266	    for p in &programs {
   267	        let args = p.args.iter().map(|a| Ok((a.name.clone(), Kind::of(&a.type_.kind)?, a.type_.optional))).collect::<R<Vec<_>>>();
   268	        if let Ok(args) = &args {
   269	            module.args.insert(p.name.clone(), args.clone());
   270	        }
   271	        signatures.insert(p.name.clone(), args);
   272	    }
   273	    for p in &programs {
   274	        let result = signatures[&p.name].clone().and_then(|args| program(&module, &helper_names, p, &args));
   275	        module.programs.insert(p.name.clone(), result);
   276	    }
   277	    Ok(module)
   278	}

   130	Spellings are illustrative. None of the blocks below is a compiling example.
   131	
   132	### 3.0 Aggregate target identity and migration
   133	
   134	Every ordinary maintained aggregate row has one internal identity function:
   135	64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from SHA-256 over the domain
   136	`snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1` and the typed canonical group-key vector.
   137	The checker therefore admits the largest legal group key against a fixed-size
   138	identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
   139	adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
   140	address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.
   141	
   142	The store metadata marker `maintained_id_version = sha256-v1` binds persisted
   143	aggregate targets to that function. Opening or adopting a store without the
   144	marker — including a 0.4.28 store whose ids were the unbounded canonical JSON
   145	of the group key — atomically clears and rebuilds every ordinary aggregate
   146	target from its source rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic
   147	generation. A failure rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation
   148	together. Adoption advice counts that rebuild even when schema/program bytes
   149	are unchanged. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
   150	`maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
   151	it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
   152	zero.
   153	
   154	### 3.1 F1: maintained columns

   157	on the post and ruling 29's hour index, Trending becomes one merge over 25 hour
   158	lanes (§21.3 P3):

     3	/-!
     4	# Rows, stores, rules and visibility
     5	
     6	A store maps each table name to its rows. Rules are evaluated against the
     7	whole store: an `exists t[..]` probe is an exact-key existence test that does
     8	not consult `t`'s own read rule (OPEN R1). A row is *visible* to a viewer
     9	when its table's read rule holds for it; every read the evaluator performs
    10	goes through `visibleRows`, so the read semantics in `Eval.lean` never sees
    11	a hidden row (`Disclosure.lean`).
    12	-/

    14	namespace Quarry
    15	
    16	structure Row where
    17	  id : List Nat
    18	  cols : List (String × Scalar)
    19	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
    20	
    21	def Row.get (r : Row) (c : String) : Scalar :=
    22	  if c = "id" then .id r.id else (r.cols.lookup c).getD .null
    23	
    24	def Row.toValue (r : Row) : Value :=
    25	  .row (("id", .s (.id r.id)) :: r.cols.map fun p => (p.1, .s p.2))
    26	
    27	/-- The store: the rows of each table. -/
    28	abbrev Store := String → List Row
    29	
    30	def Store.empty : Store := fun _ => []
    31	
    32	def Store.set (s : Store) (t : String) (rs : List Row) : Store :=
    33	  fun t' => if t' = t then rs else s t'
    34	
    35	def Store.insertRow (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : Store := s.set t (s t ++ [r])
    36	def Store.replaceRow (s : Store) (t : String) (old nw : Row) : Store :=
    37	  s.set t ((s t).map fun r => if r.id = old.id then nw else r)
    38	def Store.removeRow (s : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Store :=
    39	  s.set t ((s t).filter fun r => r.id ≠ old.id)
    40	
    41	/-- The images a rule may name. -/
    42	structure Imgs where
    43	  self : Option Row := none
    44	  old : Option Row := none
    45	  next : Option Row := none
    46	
    47	def Imgs.get (im : Imgs) : Img → Option Row
    48	  | .self => im.self
    49	  | .old => im.old
    50	  | .next => im.next
    51	
    52	def Term.eval (v : List Nat) (im : Imgs) : Term → Option Scalar
    53	  | .col i c => (im.get i).map (·.get c)
    54	  | .viewer => some (.id v)
    55	  | .param _ => none
    56	  | .lit x => some x
    57	
    58	/-- Evaluate every component of a key probe. -/
    59	def probeTerms (v : List Nat) (im : Imgs) (key : List (String × Term)) :
    60	    Option (List (String × Scalar)) :=
    61	  key.mapM fun p => Option.map (fun x => (p.1, x)) (p.2.eval v im)
    62	
    63	/-- Null returns no row only when it occurs in the selected unique point key.
    64	Nullable equalities outside that key are residual predicates and may match
    65	null. An empty `point` keeps the older all-components convention for the
    66	hand-written core model. -/
    67	def probeKey (v : List Nat) (im : Imgs) (point : List String)
    68	    (key : List (String × Term)) :
    69	    Option (List (String × Scalar)) :=
    70	  match probeTerms v im key with
    71	  | none => none
    72	  | some ks =>
    73	    let selected := if point.isEmpty then ks else ks.filter fun p => point.contains p.1
    74	    if selected.length == (if point.isEmpty then ks.length else point.eraseDups.length)
    75	        && !(selected.any fun p => p.2 == .null)
    76	    then some ks else none

    78	def keyMatch (ks : List (String × Scalar)) (r : Row) : Bool :=
    79	  ks.all fun p => decide (r.get p.1 = p.2)

   334	fn table_json(t: &ast::TableDecl, shape: &Table, tables: &[Table]) -> R<Json> {
   335	    let mut rules: BTreeMap<&str, Json> = BTreeMap::new();
   336	    if t.public.is_some() {
   337	        rules.insert("read", json!("allow"));
   338	    }
   339	    for r in &t.rules {
   340	        let word = r.effect.word();
   341	        if rules.contains_key(word) {
   342	            return no("rule-repeated", format!("{} has two {word} rules", t.name));
   343	        }
   344	        let ctx = RuleCtx { table: shape, tables };
   345	        let json = match (r.effect, r.bindings.as_slice()) {
   346	            (Effect::Update, []) => {
   347	                // OPEN R2: an unnamed update rule judges both images.
   348	                json!({"and": [ctx.rule(&r.value, &Images::As("old"))?, ctx.rule(&r.value, &Images::As("next"))?]})
   349	            }
   350	            (Effect::Update, [old, next]) => ctx.rule(&r.value, &Images::Named { old: old.clone(), next: next.clone() })?,
   351	            (_, []) => ctx.rule(&r.value, &Images::As("self"))?,
   352	            _ => return no("rule-bindings", format!("{} {word} rule bindings", t.name)),
   353	        };
   354	        rules.insert(word, json);
   355	    }
   356	    let rule = |w: &str| rules.get(w).cloned().unwrap_or(json!("deny"));
   357	    Ok(json!({
   358	        "name": t.name,
   359	        "cols": shape.cols.iter().map(|c| {
   360	            let mut col = json!({"name": c.name, "nullable": c.nullable});
   361	            if let (Kind::Id(IdSort::Ref(target)), Some(action)) = (&c.kind, c.on_delete) {
   362	                col["ref"] = json!(target);
   363	                col["onDelete"] = json!(action);
   364	            }
   365	            col
   366	        }).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
   367	        "uniques": shape.uniques,
   368	        "uniqueCodes": shape.codes,
   369	        "caps": shape.caps.iter().map(|(max, by)| json!({"by": by, "max": max})).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
   370	        "notBefore": t.not_before.as_ref().map(|(column, _)| column),
   371	        "expire": t.expire.as_ref().map(|(column, _)| column),
   372	        "read": rule("read"), "insert": rule("insert"), "update": rule("update"), "delete": rule("delete"),
   373	    }))
    15	};

codex
I found two more concrete defects: Postgres reopen does not migrate legacy aggregate ids before the shared writer switches to digest ids, and the Lean sweep can undo an earlier set-null when one child has multiple references to the deleted closure. The new ungrouped migration test also requires syntax that the committed parser still rejects.

NOT READY

- **Sweep starvation across tables.** In `20e7c22d11`, [engine/mod.rs:618](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/mod.rs:618) always starts with the first table and wraps within it. With one restricted due row there, every `limit = 1` call revisits that blocker; due rows in later tables are never reached. [through_activation.rs:453](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/through_activation.rs:453) repeats this defect for memory and Postgres.

- **Legacy Postgres aggregates are not migrated.** In `20e7c22d11`, [postgres/mod.rs:141](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/mod.rs:141) opens existing stores without rebuilding aggregate ids or publishing the identity marker and generation. The shared [schema.rs:1752](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/schema.rs:1752) nevertheless switches subsequent writes to digest addresses. Those writes cannot find the existing legacy total and use zero as their base.

- **Ungrouped migration coverage depends on implementation absent from these commits.** [retirement.rs:132](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/store/adoption_tests/retirement.rs:132) introduces `view total: count entries`, but the parser at both scoped revisions still requires `by` and a group expression ([parser.rs:781](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/parser.rs:781)). This test fails during compilation and never checks the required empty-tuple identity or `$global` discriminator.

- **Lean sweep set-null writes overwrite earlier clears.** In `f5adbda0d1`, [Write.lean:230](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Write.lean:230) takes each child image from the original `witnesses` store. If a child has two set-null references into the deleted closure, clearing the second replaces the entire row using its original image, restoring the first reference. The model leaves a dangling reference and disagrees with the engine’s current-image writes.
